docs.title: Pack the order (scan and pack)
docs.text: Do this at least two hours before the customer arrives. 8 steps.

steps.text: Select the customer's name under Ready to pack, review the order, then select Pack. Where: Pickups → Ready to pack → customer's name. You'll see: Order details: when it was placed, any pickup appointment, their services, bags to pack, items ordered, and the core and Xfinity Mobile equipment on the order. Tip: If they ordered core and Xfinity Mobile, you'll see two line items. Pack two separate bags and run scan and pack once for each.

Select Open scanner and scan the SKU on each device or piece of equipment. You'll see: Scan items: a list of everything on the order marked Not scanned. Retrieve the items and scan them in the order they appear.
Point the camera at the barcode and scan. You'll see: The scanner opens on Barcode for scan and pack. It opens on QR Code for pickups and unpacks. You can also switch to Manual.

Read the confirmation after each scan. You'll see: Success: a green check and “Scanned”. It closes by itself after five seconds, or select Close. Heads up: Error: a red ! that stays on screen. Select Retry when you're ready to scan a different device.

Review the scanned items, then select Add items. You'll see: Add to account: each item with its MAC address, IMEI or SIM. Add items adds the equipment to the customer's account. Tip: If an item gets dropped or damaged after you scanned it, select Replace on that line and scan the new one.

Select Open scanner and scan your printer to print the packing slip. You'll see: “Items were added to the customer's order.” On orders with several devices, each one is listed with its own Replace button and a Print slip button. Tip: Scan the printer you want to print to.

Select Done, attach the slip, and store the order securely. Where: Core orders: attach the slip to the bag and put it in the staging cart at the front of the house. Mobile orders: attach the slip to the bag, or wrap it around the device with a rubber band, and store it where your store keeps devices (safe room, old-style safe, or the set-aside back-of-house area). You'll see: Finish path — “That's a wrap!” Select Finish.

Check that the customer moved to the Packed queue. You'll see: The order is ready for pickup. Heads up: Look at Ready to pack one more time. If the customer has a second order (core or mobile), pack that one too.

docs.title: Complete the pickup
docs.text: When the customer arrives, check them in. The order should be in Packed. Find out whether it's a quick pickup or a consultative appointment. If the order isn't packed yet, pack it first, then come back here. 12 steps.

steps.text: Select the customer's name in the Packed queue. Where: Pickups → Packed → customer's name. Tip: Look for more than one line item. That means more than one order.
Select Check-in.

Go through the check-in form. It's filled in for you. You'll see: Guest details has the account's primary user already selected. In Visit details, the reason for visit is already Online Order Pick Up, with a BAPIS order packed banner.

Find the customer in the Waiting queue and select Start. You'll see: The session begins. A quick pickup goes to the top of the queue. An appointment is placed by appointment time. The customer's page shows a BAPIS order packed banner with how long the order stays active and that the primary account holder must pick it up. Tip: If someone else on the account checked in (not the primary account holder), the banner says the order is waiting for the primary account holder.

Select who is there for the pickup and ask for their photo ID. Heads up: Mobile orders: primary account holder only. Core orders: primary, manager or authorized user. Anyone else gets an error here (see Account owner required below). Tip: This should be the primary account holder.
Select the type of ID the customer gave you, then Next. You'll see: Customer Authentication: Photo ID or Non-photo ID.

Enter the customer's six-digit pickup code and select Verify. Heads up: Three wrong codes cancel the order. An Xfinity-provided email address can't receive the code. There is no workaround for the pickup code. Tip: The code was sent when they ordered, to the verified email on the primary account holder's profile. Need it again? Select Resend code.

After Pickup code accepted, go over the equipment with the customer. You'll see: Review order: order summary, bags to pick up, items ordered and the device details. Tip: Make sure they know what they're getting.
Select Process payment to take the customer's payment. You'll see: “Processing payment.” It can take up to four and a half minutes. When it says the process is complete, select Next.
Select Open scanner and scan the order's packing slip. You'll see: The order's bag flips from Not scanned to Scanned. Select Next.

Get the customer's signature, then select Done. You'll see: Collect signature: they can Draw it on the touchscreen or Type their name. Tip: The signature confirms they received everything and the order is correct.
Select Finish. The pickup is done. Tip: If they have a core order and a mobile order, run the pickup twice, once for each order.

docs.title: BAPIS — Scan, Pack & Pick Up: before you start
docs.text: Every BAPIS order lives in Celestial → Store Space → Pickups, sorted into three queues: Ready to pack, Packed and Unpack. Pack the order at least two hours before the customer is due in the store. Core and Xfinity Mobile bought together show up as two line items. That means two bags, and you pack and hand over each one separately. Mobile orders can only be picked up by the primary account holder. Core orders can be picked up by the primary, a manager, or an authorized user. Orders not picked up within four days move to the Unpack queue by themselves.

docs.title: BAPIS — Scan, Pack & Pick Up: good to know
docs.text: Pack early. Two hours before arrival is the rule, so a customer who walks in early isn't left waiting while you scan. Core and Mobile = two bags, two scan-and-packs, two pickups. The pickup code only goes to a verified, non-Xfinity email on the primary account holder's profile. There's no way around it. Three wrong pickup codes cancel the order. Unclaimed orders go to Unpack after four days. Unpack them so the stock goes back on the shelf. For the full Celestial packing course, see the BAPIS training in Ulearn.

docs.title: Address & identity
docs.text: Every Xfinity customer has to verify their identity before services can be ordered. 4 steps.

steps.text: Type the service address, pick it from the list, and click Continue. Where: The Let's get started screen.

Enter name, phone and email, check SMS consent, pick a language, click Next. Where: The Let's get you signed up screen. Tip: Enter the customer's first name, last name, phone number and email. Check the SMS consent box and choose English or Spanish.,If the customer gives a mobile number and opts in to texts, they get a one-time passcode to verify. That's the fastest way through.

Enter the one-time passcode from the customer's text, then click Next. You'll see: The code expires in 5 minutes. Use Resend if it didn't arrive, or I would like to verify my identity another way. Tip: Have the customer read you the code from their text.

If asked, enter Date of Birth and Social Security number, then click Next. Heads up: No SSN, or the customer doesn't want to share it? Check Alternate ID Verification. They'll have to upload a selfie holding their ID later. Tip: This is not a credit check. Say so up front, because customers worry about it.,More than 30 alternate IDs are accepted, including international documents. See *Upload documents & selfie* below.

docs.title: Internet Essentials — Agent Portal: before you start
docs.text: Be on the store's Retail WiFi. The agent portal only opens on the Comcast network. Celestial lists it as "must be on VPN", and in the store the Retail WiFi covers that. No Sales ID, no pay. Before every application, check that your Sales ID is saved in the portal. It's the same 5-digit code you use to enter sales in CSG. Have the customer there with their phone. They'll get a one-time passcode by text, and they may need to photograph a document or their ID. Don't refresh the page in the middle of an application. The applicant's data won't be saved. Quick eligibility check: Xfinity Internet is available at the address · no Xfinity Internet in the last 90 days · no Comcast debt less than a year old · on an assistance program (NSLP, housing assistance, Medicaid, SNAP, SSI and others) or household income at or below 200% of the Federal Poverty Level.

docs.title: Internet Essentials — Agent Portal: good to know
docs.text: Approvals are valid for 12 months. An existing IE customer who's moving doesn't fill out a new application. Do the transfer in CSG. IE can't be bundled. Customers can still add Xfinity TV, Xfinity Home, NOW TV, NOW TV Latino, NOW StreamSaver and Xumo Stream Box. They can't get Xfinity Flex or the Seasonal Convenience Plan. Existing TV, Mobile or Voice customers who don't have Xfinity Internet can sign up for IE. New customers get an XB6 gateway. Existing IE customers keep their XB3 unless they move tiers, and then CSG pops up an XB6 swap offer. Customers can use their own modem, but remind them the gateway is included at no cost. Application status: at internetessentials.com, customers click Application Status and enter their phone number and last name. They can also call 1-855-8-INTERNET (1-855-846-8376). If ID was verified in the store, approval can take three to five business days. If the customer still hasn't heard back after that, chat the IE team in ECM. Amnesty: a household whose only Xfinity debt is more than a year old (from the final disconnect date) can still qualify, and that old debt is forgiven. It doesn't cover Xfinity Mobile debt, and they can't upgrade or add services for a year. CSG shows a CRE pop-up with the amnesty expiration date. New York residents have additional ways to qualify (senior citizen or disability rent increase exemptions, or a utility affordability benefit). Approved customers can buy a Dell laptop for $149.99 plus tax, one per household. The Welcome Kit explains how. Dell support: 1-800-624-9896.

docs.text: Encourage the app first. Use XM360 when the customer needs you. Not for smartwatches (see section 14). For new devices, BYOD, and replacements from XMC, Apple or other makers. 9 steps. docs.title: eSIM Xfinity Mobile Activation Guide: good to know
docs.text: Most activations finish in under 10 minutes. A smartwatch can take up to 30 minutes. The eSIM QR code only works once the device is in RS (Ready State). If XM360 doesn't show RS, the QR code and the push notification won't work yet. A phone can't scan a QR code on its own screen. Show the QR on the store iPad or a computer. If the customer only has the one phone, use the manual code in section 07. eSIM to pSIM is not available. When the buy flow decides a device should use eSIM, the pSIM option is greyed out on purpose. Don't escalate eSIM→pSIM requests to ECM > XM Support. Xfinity Mobile supports one mobile service per device (Xfinity Mobile, Comcast Business Mobile or NOW Mobile), even on a dual-SIM phone. The second slot can be another carrier or a travel data plan. Billing start: BYOD eSIM and in-stock purchases bill when the order completes. Shipped devices and pSIM cards bill on delivery. Smartwatches bill at setup or 7 days after purchase, whichever is first. A one-time $25 line activation fee applies to every new phone or tablet line. Deleting an eSIM doesn't cancel the plan. Erasing the phone lets the customer choose to keep the eSIM. Never try a SIM swap or a line deactivation on a device that isn't working or doesn't seem to have an eSIM. Troubleshoot first, then escalate through standard procedures. Everything here applies to NOW Mobile customers too.

Replaces Retail360: Customer Space is where you view and manage a member's account. It brings Retail 360's functions into Celestial — the same tool you use for Point of Sale, check-in (Store Space), BAPIS and knowledge — and adds Mercury Assistant. Check in first: Check the customer in through Store Space to open their account. Check-in captures customer type, visit reason and contact info. It also helps you spot quick interactions (bill payments, exchanges), gives insight into customer needs, and surfaces sales, upgrade or support opportunities. Why it helps: All customer info in one place — less swiveling, faster visits. All customer information in one place for a personalized experience; Less time swiveling between tools; Quick summaries and answers during interactions; Faster sales, service and troubleshooting conversations.

docs.text: BYO200: Device locked by previous carrier — unlock it or pick a new device. Share How do I unlock the phone I'm bringing from my carrier? BYO1900: Carrier lock cannot be confirmed — follow the on-screen instructions. If it's confirmed locked, the customer must unlock the device or choose a new device. BYO600: Device is tied to an active line — it must be deactivated first. Tip: If you believe the error code is wrong, escalate to your supervisor. BYO800: Device is tied to a suspended line — it must be deactivated first. Tip: If you believe the error code is wrong, escalate to your supervisor. docs.title: Know the BYOD rules for new lines
crumbs: Know the BYOD rules for new lines
docs.text: Rules that apply to every bring your own device (BYOD) order: which tool to use, SIM type, compatibility results and billing start. Retail360 is retired. Place BYOD orders in XM360 — see Add a BYOD line in XM360. Smartwatch BYOD orders go through XM360 or XOE. Tablet BYOD orders go through XM360. Smartwatches use an internal eSIM that activates using the phone's IMEI.

docs.title: Customer info
crumbs: Know the BYOD rules for new lines
docs.text: Enter only the primary account holder's DOB and SSN. Heads up: It's against company policy to enter anyone else's DOB or SSN. It can affect future orders for your customer and for the person whose info was entered. When adding a new line, authenticate with the last four of the card on file. The last four of the Social Security number (SSN) won't be enough.

docs.title: Compatibility results
crumbs: Know the BYOD rules for new lines
docs.text: Good news, your device is compatible — you can move forward. The device and software are compatible and ready for switching. Both IMEI slots are checked on multi-SIM devices. If the result shows a different (alternate) IMEI, the IMEI you entered wasn't eSIM-compatible on our network, but another IMEI on the device was. You can still sign up and activate the device. If it's incompatible, here's why: Device is Incompatible: the device's technology doesn't work with our network.; Device locked: refer the customer to their current carrier to unlock it.; Unsupported operating system: have the customer connect to WiFi and install the latest iOS or Android OS.; Device reported lost or stolen: refer the customer to their current carrier.; Device active on Xfinity Mobile: the device is already active on another Xfinity Mobile line.

docs.title: SIM type
crumbs: Know the BYOD rules for new lines
docs.text: eSIM-capable devices default to eSIM; others default to pSIM. If eSIM is selected, the pSIM (nano-SIM) option is grayed out. For a pSIM, enter the SIM card's ICCID. The ICCID is on the front of the SIM card and typically begins with 89148.

docs.title: Consent and billing
crumbs: Know the BYOD rules for new lines
docs.text: Try Text message first for digital consent. If the text doesn't arrive, check the customer's phone number and resend. If that fails, use email. If they can't get either, use verbal consent. Customers have 14 days from activation to cancel without monthly charges. This applies to the lines they cancel. New customers: billing starts when the device is in hand. eSIM device or device bought in store: billing starts when the order is completed.; Device shipped: billing starts when it's delivered. Current customers: billing for the new line starts when the SIM order is placed. This is whether or not the SIM card is activated. Xfinity Mobile is billed and communicated electronically, with automatic monthly card payments. Additional fees apply if the customer cancels their Xfinity Internet. See What happens with my Xfinity Mobile account if I move to a new address or cancel my other Xfinity services?

docs.title: Activate a device on a new line in XM360
crumbs: Activate a device on a new line in XM360
docs.text: Activate an eSIM or pSIM device on a new Xfinity Mobile line in XM360, port the number if planned, and confirm it's connected. Customers get activation instructions by email and text. You can share How do I activate my mobile phone or tablet for easy-to-follow steps. Only one mobile service (Xfinity Mobile or Comcast Business Mobile) per device. This is true even on dual SIM devices. Dual SIM can still support a second line from another domestic carrier, or a local data plan when traveling outside the country. Porting a number to an existing line? Use a deferred port instead. See Port a number to an active line.

Click the refresh button to update the statuses. Updates can take up to three minutes.; Completed steps show a green checkmark.; Steps that need attention show a red exclamation mark.
Select any step that needs attention.

Use the built-in troubleshooting to fix eSIM issues. No reissue option means the issue isn't SIM-related.; Keep working through the built-in troubleshooting checklist for the customer's issue. If the customer still has trouble, reissue the eSIM when that option shows.

docs.title: Know the rules for porting a number
crumbs: Know the rules for porting a number
docs.text: What a customer needs to transfer (port) their number to Xfinity Mobile, what can't be ported, how long it takes and how promos are affected. Customers can port a wireless or landline number to a new or existing line. Don't process a port activation in Amdocs CRM — it doesn't support porting. Customers can port to an existing line any time with a deferred port. Useful when the customer decides to wait to port.; Useful when the port didn't finish at purchase.; Useful to meet a promo requirement (for example, port-in within 30 days of device activation). They can do it in the Xfinity app, or you can help in XM360. See Port a number to an active line.

docs.title: Promotions and the 30-day window
crumbs: Know the rules for porting a number
docs.text: Port trouble at activation? The customer can activate with a new number. They then have 30 days to complete the port. Counted from the new device's shipment date, or from the activation date for a BYOD. Reminders show online, in the Xfinity app, and on XM360's Devices page. The promo stays during the 30 days, then is removed if they don't port. There's a one-day buffer on day 31 for time zone differences.

docs.title: What can't be ported
crumbs: Know the rules for porting a number
docs.text: Any wireless or wireline number can be ported, except: Numbers from a different area, if the customer moved, may not be keepable. Some rural wireline providers. These providers may have special porting rules. Virtual phone numbers. From one Xfinity Mobile line to another. See how to transfer a line between Xfinity Mobile accounts. Toll-free or pager numbers with 500, 800, 888 or 900 prefixes. Numbers can't be ported to or from tablet or smartwatch lines.

docs.title: What the customer needs from their old provider
crumbs: Know the rules for porting a number
What the customer needs from their old provider
docs.text: Phone number being ported. Account number. PIN*. Account holder's name. Billing address. Last four of the account holder's SSN*. *Never share starred info with the customer by phone or chat (see the Authentication policy). Customers can enter their old provider's info at xfinitymobile.com/activate.
keywords: what the customer needs from their old provider

docs.title: Tell the customer not to…
crumbs: Know the rules for porting a number
docs.text: Cancel their old service — it must stay active for the port to work. When the port finishes, the old line closes automatically. Cancelling too early can close the account before the port finishes, and the number may be lost forever. Contact their old provider to port — unless they need their account info. Contacting them before the port finishes could close the account too early, and the number may be lost forever.

docs.title: How long a port takes
crumbs: Know the rules for porting a number
docs.text: Times depend on the account info being right — confirm it before giving an estimate. A landline can't make or receive calls while it's porting. Tell customers this before starting any activation or purchase that ports in a landline number. Stay with the customer until a wireless port is finished. Need carrier contacts or port times? Use the Carrier Details or SPID link in XM360. Xfinity Mobile supports wireless ports from more providers, including Mint Mobile, Metro by T-Mobile and Ooma. Major carriers (Verizon, AT&T, T-Mobile) — 3–5 minutes (sometimes up to 12); Smaller wireless carriers — 60 minutes to 72 hours; Wireline / landline providers — Up to 48 hours, depending on provider; Xfinity Voice — About 48 hours; VOIP (Google Fi, Vonage) — About 24 hours.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
crumbs: Know the rules for porting a number
docs.text: Update the port info in XM360, or ask the customer to update it at xfinitymobile.com/activate. Don't cancel: Don't cancel an existing port request while troubleshooting. The customer would have to wait 24 hours to resubmit. The customer doesn't know their current provider account or PIN. — Review the list of provider porting details to help find it.; The customer gets an error porting through the activation portal. — Review port failure cases to figure out the error.; The customer isn't the account holder and wants to start the port. — Have them contact the primary account holder to start it. Only the primary user and/or account holder can sign in with their Xfinity ID.; The customer got an email or text about an issue. — Review account cases to confirm the error or message sent.; The customer wants to cancel the port and get a new number, and the port hasn't processed or has failed. — Cancel the port if needed, then select the New Number option in XM360.; The customer wants to port their number from Xfinity Mobile to another provider. — Care agents transfer the customer to XM Security PIN Support - (Port Out) in OneCTI for the Security PIN, account number and ZIP code.

docs.title: Check if an Xfinity Voice number can port
crumbs: Check if an Xfinity Voice number can port
docs.text: Check whether a customer's Xfinity Voice home phone number can be ported to a new Xfinity Mobile line. An Xfinity Voice number ported to a new mobile line counts as a new line. The line may qualify for Xfinity Mobile promotions that require a port-in. Xfinity Voice ports take about 48 hours.

docs.title: Check the number
crumbs: Check if an Xfinity Voice number can port
docs.text: 5 steps.

docs.text: Enter a customer's old-carrier details so their current number ports to a new Xfinity Mobile or Comcast Business Mobile line, and read the port status. Stay with the customer until you confirm the number works. Do not let them leave (or hang up) until the port is complete. Don't process port-in activations in Amdocs CRM. Also works for Comcast Business Mobile customers.

docs.title: Submit and activate
docs.text: 4 steps.

steps.text: Check that the MDN field shows the right phone number.

Select Activate. You'll see: Status shows "Activation Processing". Find it on the Devices tab and the Activation Status tab in the Notification Center. Stay with the customer. Wait three to five minutes, then refresh the page.
Watch the status until it shows Port successful. Tip: Status meanings are in Port statuses below.
Activation pending over 12 minutes? Check MySyniverse/Crossroads. If it still says pending there, open an XM Support case in ECM > Activation/porting > Porting error.

docs.title: Port statuses
docs.text: Starting: Starting activation. Pending: Port pending... awaiting response — the request is being reviewed. If it's still there after five minutes, it's still processing. You may need to wait another five to seven minutes. Confirmed: Port confirmed... activation pending — nothing else needed. It completes by the due date and time in the Port Confirmation banner. The customer gets an email when it's done. Error: Resolution required/Activation error — fix the fields and resubmit. The port failed. Follow the steps in the banner, update the fields in XM360 and submit the port again. Yellow banners can be corrected. Red banner: Red banner: open an XM Support case in ECM. Pick Activation/porting.; Choose Porting errors. Tip: Failed landline (wireline) port? You can resubmit in XM360. DDT defaults to 72 hours (about six days). Some roles can extend the due date and time for weekends, holidays or old-provider delays. Done: Port successful — the number is active and ready to use.

docs.title: Landline (wireline) ports
docs.text: Most take 48 to 72 hours (about six days); some take 7 to 10 days. Confirm with the customer that no activation is needed. Set clear expectations about the wait before they leave.

docs.title: Avoid porting errors
docs.text: XM360 accepts letters, numbers and special characters in most fields, but wrong formatting causes errors. Porting MDN: 10 digits only, no special characters. Double-check for extra spaces in name and address fields. Schema failed validation means something's in the wrong format. The port may get stuck in MySyniverse/Crossroads and won't be accepted by the RSSX/XM Network Management Tool. Common error codes: 6C — Customer information does not match; 8A — Account number required or incorrect; 8C — Password/PIN required or incorrect; 8D — ZIP code required or incorrect; 8E — First name required or incorrect; 8F — Last name required or incorrect. For more, check Xfinity Mobile porting error codes.

docs.title: Field-by-field tips
docs.text: Account number: Varies by carrier; may mix numbers and letters. Letters must be capitalized. Example: Verizon prepaid account numbers are 12 characters, like A01234567890. The first "A" is needed and must be capitalized — a lowercase "a" causes an error. New customers can get it from Verizon Wireless customer service at 1-800-922-0204. PIN / password: Numbers, letters or both; any case. No PIN? Enter a space. Still failing after updating the PIN? Check MySyniverse/Crossroads to confirm the PIN is correct. If it matches in both, contact the Original Service Provider (OSP) with the customer to verify the PIN, or have the customer contact their provider. Customers can check their PIN in their provider's app, website or customer service. Some PINs expire in 24 hours, others in seven days, depending on the provider. Leaving the field blank makes XM360 auto-fill it with "PASSWORD". When you pick a provider, the Account Holder Info section shows how to get the right PIN. Last 4 SSN: Enter the last four of the customer's SSN in Last 4 SSN. To fix it: Don't cancel or deny the port request. Start a three-way call with Consumer Cellular and the customer, or have the customer call and request a manual response to the port request. Consumer Cellular often needs the SSN, but it doesn't pass to MySyniverse/Crossroads. That causes a Delay status and a 6G (Port Complexity) error, then Resolution required in MySyniverse/Crossroads and 6C (Customer information does not match) in XM360. Name: Enter first and last name exactly as the old provider has it. Business account: put the business…

crumbs: Port a number to an active line (deferred port)
docs.text: Transfer a customer's number from another provider onto an Xfinity Mobile line that's already active, in XM360. Porting to a brand-new line instead? See Enter porting info in XM360. Confirm the number is active with the customer's current provider. The customer must use a different device than the one getting the number. If the customer can't complete SIM OTA Provisioning, don't submit a deferred port with the number already active on the line as a workaround.; Switching numbers between devices on the account? Use the MDN swap process.; Moving a line between Xfinity Mobile accounts? See how to transfer a line between Xfinity Mobile accounts. Make sure the customer has their old provider's account details. Port protection / number lock must be turned off. All details must be 100% right to prevent porting issues and service disruptions. Tell the customer their voicemail won't carry over. Once the number changes, the old voicemail mailbox stops working and their voicemails are lost. Port within 30 days of activation to qualify for a promo. Enter the old provider's details. Primary account holder's first name, last name and last four of their SSN; Account number, Number Transfer PIN and billing address. Tip: Field tips: Enter porting info in XM360. Need help finding them? See find account information from previous service providers.

To do this, I will have to temporarily deactivate the line of service and then reactivate it with the ported number. Do I have your permission to begin the porting process?".

docs.title: Process an upgrade anytime (phone still on a DPP)
crumbs: Process an upgrade anytime (phone still on a DPP)
docs.text: Upgrade an eligible customer's phone that isn't paid off yet, with the DPP waived and a guaranteed discount on the new phone. Upgrade anytime is only for eligible plans. It's exclusively for Xfinity Mobile customers on the latest pricing plan enrolled in the Mobile Plus plan, and Premium Unlimited customers on the fifth generation pricing plan (previously known as Elite Upgrade). Customers can upgrade even if the phone isn't paid off. Unlike early upgrade, they don't need 50% paid off or an upgrade fee, and their current device payment plan is waived. Upgrade anytime combines the benefits of an enhanced early upgrade and NDEL. They get a guaranteed discount off their next phone on a DPP. The order can be canceled within 30 minutes, before fulfillment. See the *Cancel an Xfinity Mobile order before fulfillment* article. A trade-in can't be reversed once we take the device. Heads up: Once we take ownership or possession of the device, the device trade-in can't be reversed. Compare options and current deals before you start. See *Mobile promotions* for the latest offers, and the *differences between upgrade anytime, early upgrade, and NDEL* article for trade-in options. Only the Account Holder, Primary, or Manager Xfinity ID users can do this. Phone already paid off? Use the paid-in-full steps.

crumbs: Activate a paired smartwatch in XM360
docs.text: Activate a smartwatch that pairs to the customer's phone (Smartwatch fee) and download its eSIM in XM360. Requirement: Needs an available line and an active XM phone on the same OS. The phone must use the same operating system as the watch. This applies to both the Smartwatch Data Plan (standalone) and the Smartwatch fee (paired device). Timing: Tell the customer setup can take up to 30 minutes. It involves Bluetooth pairing, app downloads and cellular setup. The exact time depends on the apps the customer downloads and the device's operating system. Update first: Have the customer update the software on both the phone and the watch. Also make sure the devices are compatible — see the Smartwatches (GPS + cellular) with Xfinity Mobile overview. Try the app: Encourage the customer to try the watch app first. Share How do I activate my smartwatch? with them before you activate in XM360. Need a line: No watch line yet? Add one first. See Add a smartwatch line in XM360. You can also share How do I add a line to my Xfinity Mobile account? Finish on watch: After activating in XM360, the customer still turns on cellular data on the watch. Follow Step 2: Cellular activation in How do I activate my smartwatch?

Timing: Tell the customer setup can take up to 30 minutes. It involves Bluetooth pairing, app downloads and cellular setup. You can also share How do I add a line to my Xfinity Mobile account? Finish on watch: After activating in XM360, the customer still turns on cellular data on the watch. docs.title: Fix common smartwatch issues
docs.text: Quick checks for smartwatch activation errors, "Watch is Busy," eSIM and Galaxy watch text issues. Xfinity ID: Make sure the customer uses the right Xfinity ID. Use the Xfinity ID tied to the line, or the Primary or Manager's Xfinity ID, to activate the watch. Check Users and Preferences in Einstein 360 to find it. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360. Carrier settings: Have the customer tap Update now for carrier settings. Apple: Settings > General > About.; Android: Settings > About phone > Software update > Download and install. The phone shows a message when carrier settings need an update. eSIM not showing: "No eSIM installed" while paired is normal. The eSIM appears once the phone is turned off or out of range. We own it: Don't send customers to the manufacturer for activation issues. Activation problems are handled by us, not the device manufacturer. Watch is Busy: "Watch is Busy" but active in XM360? Restart both devices a few times. Still stuck? Factory reset the watch only, then try again.; If a reset doesn't work, reassign the eSIM — see Redownload a smartwatch eSIM. Don't remove: Don't remove the Xfinity Mobile line from the watch app. Heads up: Removing it can cause "Uh-oh!" or "Watch is Busy" on setup — the watch may still be linked to the old MDN. Galaxy texts: Galaxy watch texts may show the watch's number. docs.title: Fix a smartwatch that won't charge
crumbs: Fix a smartwatch that won't charge
docs.text: Walk the customer through charging checks and a force restart when their watch won't charge. 5 steps.

steps.text: Check for the lightning bolt icon when the charger is connected. A lightning bolt shows when the watch needs to charge. If the screen is blank or shows the Magnetic Charging Cable icon, charge it for up to 30 minutes.

Check the cable is fully plugged into the adapter and the wall. Always use the original Magnetic Charging Cable and USB power adapter that came with the watch.; Remove any plastic covers from the charger and place it flat on the back of the watch.

Still not charging? Force restart the watch. Apple watch: Hold the side button and Digital Crown for at least 10 seconds, or until the Apple logo shows.; Samsung watch: Hold the Power (Home) and Back buttons together until "Rebooting..." shows. Don't select Power off on the screen or Restart when it appears. It may take up to 30 seconds for "Rebooting..." to appear.
Check for software updates.
Try a different charging cable and USB power adapter. If the battery is empty, it may take a few minutes before the watch turns back on.

docs.title: Know tablet plans and eligibility
docs.text: Know-this-first guide to Xfinity Mobile tablet pricing, eligibility, fees and common customer questions. Apple iPads and select Samsung tablets are sold through Xfinity Mobile. Available since December 10, 2025. Customers can also bring their own compatible Apple iPad or Samsung tablet. Where: Buy at Xfinity Retail Stores, xfinitymobile.com or over the phone. How to pay: Pay in full or with a device payment plan (DPP). Price: Tablet Unlimited is $20 per month per line (5th and 6th gen plans). On 6th gen plans, each tablet and smartwatch has a fee. If the combined tablet and watch cost is more than $35, an All-in Tablet & Watch Plan credit is applied at the bottom of the bill. It covers up to 10 tablet and/or watch lines. Taxes and fees still apply. Benefits: Tablets stay connected away from WiFi with cellular data. Customers can browse the web, send email, access files and more on the go. See all tablets on the Xfinity Mobile tablet shop page. BYO: Check BYO tablets with the IMEI compatibility tool. See the Xfinity Mobile BYOD overview for compatibility details.

docs.title: Plan comparison
docs.text: Data: After the data threshold, speeds are no longer prioritized. Activation: $25 line activation fee applies to all plans. Fees may be waived during promotions. Hotspot: Personal hotspot isn't available on tablets. Travel: No international data roaming on tablets. The Mexico and Canada Unlimited Pass and Global Travel Pass aren't supported. Customers can use WiFi abroad; cellular data in Mexico and Canada is charged pay as you go. Price — Tablet Unlimited $20/mo per line — $10 Tablet Line Fee per line, on top of the 4th gen mobile plan — $45/mo per line; Premium data — 15 GB 5G+ — By the Gig & Unlimited: 20 GB 5G. Unlimited Premium: 50 GB 5G — 20 GB 5G; XMC — $9 to $19 by device (XMC Plus included with one Mobile Plus line) — $9 to $19 by device — $9 to $19 by device; Video — HD (720p) — By the Gig & Unlimited Premium: HD (720p). Unlimited: SD (480p) — SD (480p).

docs.title: Eligibility
docs.text: The Xfinity Mobile credit screening policy applies. Customers must buy or bring a tablet and add a new line. A tablet can be the only line on an account. Tablet-only accounts don't qualify for the multi-product discount (MPD). Tablets are XMC eligible. With one Mobile Plus line on the latest pricing plan, XMC Plus covers all watches and tablets on the account. See the XMC overview. Numbers can't be ported into or out of tablet lines.

docs.title: Fees
docs.text: Tablet line fee: 4th gen plans pay a $10/month tablet line fee per active tablet. This is on top of any DPP charges and data use. If the customer cancels the line to stop the fee, they lose any remaining promo device credits and still owe the remaining DPP balance. Activation fee: A $25 line activation fee applies when a new line is added and activated. Since June 26, 2025 (phones and tablets only). It replaced the one-time $25 setup fee charged since March 22, 2024.; Shows on the first bill for new customers, or the next XM bill for existing customers.; Doesn't apply when replacing or upgrading a device on an existing line.; Does apply if a customer cancels a line and adds a new one later.; May be waived during promotions. Not charged for smartwatches. California: California: see California embedded battery fee and e-waste fee.

docs.title: Customer questions
docs.text: BYO tablet?: Yes, customers can bring a compatible iPad or Samsung tablet. See the Xfinity Mobile BYOD overview. Cancel line?: Canceling the tablet line ends any remaining subsidy. Remaining DPP charges may be accelerated onto the next Xfinity Mobile bill. See the policy on canceling lines. Cellular vs WiFi: Cellular tablets use the cellular network; WiFi-only tablets use WiFi only. Move a SIM?: No — use the SIM that came with the new iPad. Follow the activation guide. Moving a SIM from another tablet or phone gives an "Unable to activate cellular network" error. Text messages?: No texting — tablet plans are internet only. Voice and text plans aren't available for tablets, but iPads can send and receive iMessages with other compatible Apple devices. Hotspot?: No — tablet plans don't support hotspot use. See Xfinity's Mobile Broadband Disclosures.

Available for XM and Comcast Business Mobile (CBM) customers. Before, only Apple tablets were offered through XM. When: Started December 10, 2025. For you: Offer new Samsung tablets or BYOD Android tablets. Customers can now choose between Android and Apple tablets. Price: $20 per month per tablet line, plus the $25 line activation fee.

docs.title: Eligibility
docs.text: New or BYOD Android devices. New and existing XM residential customers. CBM customers. Payment: Pay in full, 36-month DPP, or device promotions. Review the latest mobile promotions for current tablet deals.

Purchase and activate Android tablets as an XM tablet line. Customers and reps can both do this. For more, see Know tablet plans and eligibility. docs.title: Fix Business Mobile XOE issues (FAQs)
docs.text: Quick answers for common Comcast Business Mobile problems in XOE: eligibility, My Account, upgrades, errors, fraud review, crashes, financing, and who to call. Call the COE at 844-963-0206, weekends included. This is the Comcast Business Mobile XOE support path.

docs.title: Can I sell before Business Internet is installed?
crumbs: Can I sell before Business Internet is installed?
docs.text: Sometimes a pending Business Internet install stops mobile transactions from completing. Watch for eligibility, financing, or upgrade errors. You may see eligibility issues, unexpected errors, financing issues, or upgrade restrictions when Business Internet has not been completed. Check if the Business Internet install is still pending. Check that the customer activated their My Account profile. Review current defect communications or workaround guidance. Retry after the Business Internet install is done, when appropriate. Installed and still failing? Escalate. Include the account number, Session ID, Visitor Session ID, screenshots, and a short description of the issue.

crumbs: Does the customer need My Account first?
docs.text: Yes. Many ordering, consent, and approval steps depend on My Account access. Confirm My Account is activated. Confirm the customer can get into My Account. Not working? Engage the Center of Excellence (COE). Use the approved Retail process. Retry the mobile transaction once access is confirmed.

crumbs: Can I do upgrades and NDELs in store now?
docs.text: Yes. The in-store NDEL and upgrade fix launched September 15, 2026. You can scan in-store inventory through the plan-led flow. Applies to new lines and upgrades or NDELs. Start in Celestial and launch into XOE. See Open a Business account in XOE. Confirm every existing device on the account is activated. If any device isn't activated, complete the activation before trying the upgrade. New lines: use store inventory when available. Upgrades: use ship-to-home fulfillment. See Upgrade or exchange a Business Mobile device. Still stuck? Capture escalation details and follow the Retail support path.

docs.title: How to position it
crumbs: Sell Business Mobile Standard and Pro plans
docs.text: Lead with Pro: Pro is the best overall experience for most businesses. “For most businesses, Pro is the best fit because it’s built for performance in busy moments.”; “Pro keeps your team moving with fewer slowdowns, plus stronger hotspot and video support.”. It removes tradeoffs: unlimited premium data, stronger performance in busy moments, better hotspot and high-quality video support, and international features built in. Standard: Use Standard for price-focused or lighter-usage customers. “Standard is a great fit if you want a strong value plan with a simple, predictable setup.”; “Standard covers everyday business needs without extra complexity.”. docs.title: Change a phone number (MDN) in XM360
crumbs: Change a phone number (MDN) in XM360
docs.text: Give a line a new random number, or swap in a ported number, from the Devices page in XM360. Always try XM360 first. Go over these with the customer before you start. Spam calls: If it's for robo/spam calls, suggest blocking those calls first. Voicemail: Their voicemail box stops working and saved voicemails are lost. After the change, rebuild the mailbox. See Fix voicemail after a number change. Inactive device: If the device is inactive, the number may change to an Xfinity-created number. Off the phone: Make sure the customer is not on the device. This keeps the call from disconnecting when the number changes. No picking numbers: We can't honor requests for a specific number or area code. The exception is porting in an existing number.; Numbers are assigned randomly from available numbers based on the customer's ZIP code.; The new number may have a different area code than someone else's number in the same area. Once in 30 days: A line's number can only be changed once every 30 days. Heads up: If the number was changed in the last 30 days, don't submit the XM Support case in ECM. A second try within 30 days gives an error in both XM360 and the XM Network Troubleshooting Tool. Porting: Porting a number to an active line is a deferred port. Don't try to process an MDN port activation in Amdocs CRM. CRM doesn't support porting.

docs.title: Transfer a line to another Xfinity Mobile account
crumbs: Transfer a line to another Xfinity Mobile account
docs.text: Move an active line — device and number — from one Xfinity Mobile account to another in XM360. Both account holders, or a Primary user or Manager from both accounts, must be available. Both accounts: Valid payment method on file and no past-due balance. Both accounts must be on the same plan generation.; If generations differ, the receiving and sending accounts may need to move to the current generation. Changing plans may affect data options, pricing, discounts and promotions.; Neither account can be involved in fraud or acceptable use policy violations. Target account: Must be eligible to add a new line. If the device has an existing DPP, the target account must be eligible for a DPP and have the required DPP dollar amount available. The line: No pending orders; active two full billing cycles; first bill paid. Tip: A paired smartwatch can now transfer with the line. Pending orders include a device pre-order or backorder. The device: Not returnable, not lost/stolen, and paired to the line's SIM. Must not be eligible for a return or exchange.; Must not be reported lost or stolen.; Must be paired to the SIM of the line being transferred. If the SIM is paired but the old device still shows, the customer can set up the phone on that line from the Devices page (BYOD). If they can't, use a BYONDEL upgrade (or eSIM BYONDEL upgrade) in XM360. Internet: Needs active Xfinity Internet, or be eligible for a Mobile-only line. Bulk customers are eligible for Xfinity Mobile.; Xfinity On Campus and Managed WiFi customers aren't eligible.

docs.title: Before you start
crumbs: Transfer a line to another Xfinity Mobile account
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: Check which plan generation each account is on. Heads up: If generations differ, don't promise either account can go back to its prior generation. Review the plan change, pricing, data options, promotions and monthly charges with the customer before continuing.
Confirm the customer meets the requirements above.
Confirm the target account has a valid payment method. Where: Target account in XM360: switch from Sales to Care, then Billing → Payment Method.
Check whether any promotions won't transfer. Some promotions may not transfer. Check the promotion's terms and conditions.

Get consent from both the target and source account. The target account holder must: Fully authenticate. Provide a valid line transfer PIN from the source account. Verbally consent to the transfer and any new monthly charges tied to the line (DPP installments, Xfinity Mobile Care, active promotions). Heads up: Don't help with a transfer if the caller can't authenticate or the account has a Compromised flag. Tip: If the source account holder is deceased, follow the death of a customer account policy. Speak to the account holder or Primary user (or a Manager) on both accounts.

docs.title: Tell the customer
crumbs: Transfer a line to another Xfinity Mobile account
docs.text: Share these disclosures before transferring. Transferring may change the plan, monthly cost, discounts, promotions or features. Prorated: XMC premiums, Unlimited data options, line fees and device charges are prorated. Line fees include the tablet line fee and line access fee. Not prorated: By the Gig usage before the transfer bills to the source account. History: Usage, call/text logs, payments and statements don't transfer. After the transfer, My Account on xfinitymobile.com and the Xfinity app show only post-transfer activity. AppleCare+: AppleCare+ from Xfinity Mobile stays active on the device. Coverage is 24 months from the original purchase date. Customers can check their Proof of Coverage email for details and claims. Line limit: If the target account is at max lines, the line can't transfer. No exceptions. See the Xfinity Mobile credit screening policy. PIN: A transfer PIN goes to the account that currently has the line.

docs.title: Transfer the line in XM360
crumbs: Transfer a line to another Xfinity Mobile account
docs.text: For accounts with active lines. If the source account has no active lines, it's a Change of Ownership instead — see Escalations. 17 steps.

steps.text: On the target account, go to Line & Data → Transfer lines to this account. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.
Get the transfer details from the target account holder. Mobile numbers (MDNs) to transfer.; Source account holder's account number, contact number or email address.
Click Continue once you have all the information.
Enter the MDN to transfer.
Ask about any smartwatch paired to that number. Check if the customer wants to transfer or disconnect it.
Confirm the source account holder's contact number, email or account number.
Click Submit.
Review the transfer details and the customer consent. Add any other MDNs to transfer, and choose to transfer or disconnect paired smartwatches.
Click Continue. The transfer PIN goes to the source account holder's contact info on file and must be redeemed within five days.
A credit check runs. Click Continue. It confirms the target account can add the line(s). Results are valid for 60 days.
Choose a mobile plan for the line, then select Next.

If Mobile Plus was added, read the pop-up, then Continue. Tell the customer Xfinity Mobile Care Plus covers their phone and all eligible tablets and watches on the account. Any XMC overage for currently enrolled devices is canceled. XMC Plus renews month-to-month until canceled.

Review the order, get approval, then select Start transfer request. Try digital approval first. If it must be verbal, follow how to get verbal approval or supervisor assistance with verbal approval for XM360 orders.

When the source holder gets the PIN, click Enter PIN. The PIN is required for every XM360 line transfer.; It's sent by text message and email.; A screen shows the timeframe for redeeming it. If it runs out, submit a new transfer request.
Enter the PIN from the customer, then click Submit. Click Request new PIN to resend it if needed.; This page also shows the MDN and IMEI of any lines still being transferred.

Review the transfer result for each line. Success — confirm the line is on the target account and review the new setup.; Failure — review the reason and follow troubleshooting or escalation.; Transferring — let it finish and refresh the status.; Transfer pending — explain processing isn't done and follow any XM360 message.
Check the source account's activity timeline if needed. It shows the completed transfer, the PIN that was sent, and a banner while a transfer is in progress.

docs.title: Switch a customer from Xfinity Mobile to NOW Mobile
crumbs: Switch a customer from Xfinity Mobile to NOW Mobile
docs.text: Offer NOW Mobile when a customer wants to cancel Xfinity Mobile, then run the switch eligibility check in XM360. If a customer asks to cancel Xfinity Mobile, offer NOW Mobile to keep them. Needs internet: Customer must be in the Xfinity footprint with Xfinity Internet or NOW Internet. Not both: Customers can't have Xfinity Mobile and NOW Mobile at the same time. Current Xfinity Mobile customers can downgrade to NOW Mobile at any time (eligibility restrictions apply). 60-day lock: Devices must be active 60 days before switching. Applies to devices bought from Xfinity Mobile and BYOD devices. No DPPs: NOW Mobile has no device payment plans. The customer pays the remaining balance on their Xfinity Mobile device (if any). No wearables: Wearables aren't available with NOW Mobile. Good standing: No past-due balance, suspension or collections. The Switch to NOW Mobile button is grayed out if the customer doesn't meet this.

Xfinity TV — No — Yes — No; Xfinity Internet — No — Yes — Yes; Xfinity Mobile — Yes* — No — Yes; Xfinity Home — No — Yes — Yes; Xfinity Voice — No — Yes — Yes.

docs.title: Before you cancel a line: rules & what to tell the customer
crumbs: Before you cancel a line: rules & what to tell the customer
docs.text: Read this before you cancel, cease or deactivate any Xfinity Mobile or NOW Mobile line — the rules and everything the customer must hear first. Heads up: A deactivated line may lose its phone number permanently. Only cancel when the customer asks. Customer asks only: Only cancel a line when the customer specifically requests it. An Xfinity Mobile or NOW Mobile line should never be canceled, ceased, or deactivated unless the customer specifically requests we cancel. Don't cancel a line for any other reason. Never to troubleshoot: Never deactivate a line to troubleshoot. Heads up: Line deactivation may result in the phone number being permanently lost. Only Tier 2 and higher support tiers can reconnect a ceased line using CRM. Not for transfers: Never cancel a line to transfer it or combine accounts. Never cancel a line when trying to transfer it from one Xfinity Mobile or NOW Mobile account to another, or when trying to combine accounts. Use the transfer a line between Xfinity Mobile accounts process instead. Permanent: Deactivating permanently removes the line from Xfinity Mobile service.

docs.title: Tell the customer first
crumbs: Before you cancel a line: rules & what to tell the customer
docs.text: Go over every point below before you deactivate the line. XMC ends: Xfinity Mobile Care (XMC) for the device is canceled for good. XMC coverage for the associated device will be canceled and can't be reinstated. Device payments: They keep paying monthly device payments until the device is paid off. Tip: DPPs are not available with NOW Mobile. After it's paid off, they can unlock the device and use it with another carrier. They will continue to be billed monthly for any device payment plan (DPP) balance on the line. Porting out?: To port the number to another carrier, the line must stay active. Heads up: If the line is deactivated, the number may be released and may not be available for reactivation. Promos stop: Extended promotional credits stop and won't come back if the line is reactivated. They will no longer receive the extended promotional credits on their bill after the line is deactivated, and the credits will not be applied if the line is reactivated. AppleCare+: AppleCare+ continues for two years from the original purchase date. If the device is returned within 14 days, AppleCare+ is canceled automatically and the customer receives a full refund within 60 days. See the details of AppleCare+ with Xfinity Mobile. Smartwatch: A paired smartwatch is affected too — make sure they understand. If there's a smartwatch paired with the customer's line, deactivating the line affects both the phone and the watch. See Xfinity Mobile's service cancellation policy for the full terms.

Locked device: Their device is locked to the original carrier and can't be unlocked. What it cancels: Ceasing in XM360 cancels the line everywhere it lives. docs.title: Check a device before a return or exchange
crumbs: Check a device before a return or exchange
docs.text: The checks to finish, and the return type to pick, before you start any Xfinity Mobile phone, tablet or smartwatch return or exchange. 14 days: Customers have 14 days from delivery or store purchase to return or exchange. For any reason. Devices delivered or bought in-store more than 60 days ago are not eligible for returns or exchanges. Activation: Returns don't need reactivation; exchanges still require activation. If a device arrives pre-activated or deactivated, activate the line before starting an exchange RMA. Restocking fee: Most returns and non-warranty exchanges have a $35 restocking fee. Waive the fee if the customer is deceased (see the death of a customer policy). Some taxes and fees charged at purchase may not be refunded. Who can do it: Only the Account Holder, Primary, or Manager Xfinity ID users can do this. Other users won't be able to make these changes. One per return: Only one item per return — start separate returns for multiple items.

crumbs: Check a device before a return or exchange
docs.text: Choose the Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) type that matches what the customer wants. Terminal return: Return the device and cancel the mobile line. Tip: Customers can return a pending activation new device existing line (NDEL) device, keep their current line active, and get a refund for the new device. Buyer's remorse exchange: Keep the line; exchange for a different financed (DPP) device. BYOD exchange: Keep the line; swap the purchased device for one of their own (BYO or PIF). Warranty exchange: Only within the 14-day window, and only if the device is defective (not damaged). After the 14-day window, send the customer to the device manufacturer or an authorized service center. See the Xfinity Mobile warranty support overview.

docs.title: Check the device first
crumbs: Check a device before a return or exchange
docs.text: Complete these steps before starting a Retail or Care return or exchange. 7 steps.

steps.text: Search for the account using Customer Search in XM360. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.
Go to Lines of Service and pick the line in question.
Confirm the mobile device number (MDN) and IMEI. The IMEI may show as ESN/MEID. Use the Qelp tool to find the IMEI/ESN for each device.
Run a diagnostic test on the device. Android: see Xfinity Mobile Care (XMC) by Assurant diagnostics.; Apple: see How to put your iPhone in diagnostics mode.
Run the Interactive Troubleshooting Guide (ITG) to check exchange eligibility. The article runs the ITG in Einstein 360. If the device is defective, process the RMA.
Tell the customer the device can't have any damage. For example liquid damage, unauthorized repairs, rooting or jailbreaking. If damage is found, fees may apply.
Have the customer back up and remove their personal data. Heads up: For Apple devices, Find My must be turned off. Back up any contacts and photos they want before sending the device.

docs.title: iPhone 18 Pro Max returns
crumbs: Check a device before a return or exchange
docs.text: Attach a lithium battery label to the outside of the return box. Tip: Customers can find the label in the email sent with their tracking label, or via "How do I return or exchange my mobile device and accessories?". Or follow the steps in the Apple support article to prepare the phone before shipping it for repair, trade in, or return.

docs.title: Process a return in XM360
docs.text: Return an Xfinity Mobile phone, tablet or smartwatch in XM360 within the 14-day window and refund the customer. Do the device checks first. Confirm MDN and IMEI, run diagnostics, check for damage, and have the customer remove personal data. Devices don't need reactivation to be returned. Customers have 14 days from delivery or store purchase. Devices delivered or bought more than 60 days ago aren't eligible.

docs.title: Process the return
docs.text: 11 steps.

steps.text: Open XM360. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.
Click the Orders & Returns tab.
Click Start a return or exchange.

Choose the device to return and click Continue. Only devices that qualify for returns will show.; Devices don't need reactivation for returns, but exchanges still require activation beforehand.; Devices delivered or bought in-store more than 60 days ago are not eligible. Only one item per return — start separate returns for multiple items.
Select a Return Type and Return Reason, then click Next. Tip: Let the customer know their line will be deactivated, and help them move their number.
If it's an iPhone, help the customer turn off Find My.

Answer the condition questions, then click Continue. You'll see: The Return Summary opens. Ask about the device's condition and pick the options that match the customer's answers. The form looks slightly different in Retail and Care.

NDEL pending activation? Choose to keep the current line active. For a new device on an existing line (NDEL) that's still pending activation, you can keep the customer's current line active and process a refund for the new device. This option appears after the inspection step.
Review what you entered with the customer, then click Submit return. Tip: Let the customer know refunds may take three to five business days, depending on their bank.
To see the device's grade, open Returns & Exchanges → View assessment.
To see grading criteria, click View device grade criteria.

docs.title: Customer wants a 36-month DPP instead
docs.text: For a customer who bought on a 24-month DPP within the 14 days before Xfinity switched to 36-month DPPs. Exchange: An exchange keeps the 24-month DPP. They can exchange the phone for another device, but the 24-month DPP still applies because the original order date fell before the switch. Return + new order: To get a 36-month DPP, return the device and place a new order. Customers within the 14-day remorse period can return their device purchase and place a new order for a new device on a 36-month DPP. Trade-ins: The trade-in device can't be given back once shipped or handed over. Customers who did a trade-in can still return the new phone within 14 days. See the Xfinity Mobile trade-in promotions (TIPs) overview and the integrated trade-in (fair-value credit) program overview for details.

docs.title: Process an exchange in XM360
docs.text: Exchange an Xfinity Mobile phone, tablet or smartwatch for a different device in XM360 while the customer keeps their line. Do the device checks first. Confirm MDN and IMEI, run diagnostics, check for damage, and have the customer remove personal data. Exchanges require the device to be activated first. If a device arrives pre-activated or deactivated, activate the line before starting an RMA. Customer wants a 36-month DPP? See the note in Process a return. An exchange keeps the original 24-month DPP if the order was placed before the switch to 36-month DPPs.

docs.title: Reactivate a line in XM360
docs.text: Bring back a deactivated phone, tablet or watch line on the customer's old number, usually within 30 days of deactivation. In many cases you can reactivate eligible phones, tablets and watches on the previous number within 30 days of deactivation. Not eligible: These lines can't be reactivated: Line was ceased over 30 days ago and the number was returned to the original provider.; Mobile device number (MDN) has been ported out to another provider.; Fraud-related deactivations (handled by the Fraud team; the message directs customers to a store to verify identity).; Lines in collections cease status (121 or more days of non-payment).; Customers without active Xfinity Core or Mobile accounts.; Xfinity Mobile only customers with no active lines.; Customer is at their line limit and not eligible to activate another MDN.; Paired and standalone watches need an active line on the account.; Terminal returns (devices sent back to Xfinity Mobile).

Open Devices and find the line under Deactivated on the left.
Click Reactivate line.

Not eligible? Read the message — it explains why. Fraud (role controlled): "Cannot reactivate device now — This line was ceased due to suspected fraud. The customer must visit a store and verify proof of residency and identity."; MDN ported out: "Device not eligible for reactivation — MDN was ported to another provided."; IMEI eligibility error: "Device not eligible not reactivation — Device is assigned to a different MDN and cannot be reactivated.". Lines deactivated due to fraud require the customer to verify identity in store before reactivating.
Choose the Reactivation Reason and click Continue.

Pick the data option the customer wants, then click Continue. Plan selection isn't needed for Device return or MDN Port-out reasons — XM360 auto-selects the lowest plan as part of the port-out process.; Plan selection isn't needed for tablets and watches.; A blue banner explains that promotions and Xfinity Mobile Care (XMC) won't be added when a line is reactivated, per policy.; If Line is accidentally ceased is picked, a message tells you to escalate to Enterprise Case Management (ECM) to have XMC added outside open enrollment and promos manually re-added if needed.
Wait while the reactivation is in progress.

Refresh Devices to see the line back under active lines. You'll see: The line appears under active lines on the Devices page. Tip: You'll see device payment plans (DPP) if payments remain on the reactivated line.

docs.text: Existing Xfinity Mobile lines or pending new line orders, and active core service — Existing customer account segment; At least one core service but no existing Xfinity Mobile lines — Most recent segment; Xfinity Mobile only customers — Most recent segment. Xfinity Mobile only customers on older segments must upgrade the account to the most recent segment before reactivating a line.

docs.title: Reconnect a ceased line
docs.text: How XM Repair Agents reconnect a voluntarily canceled line using RSSX or the XM Ops Tool and Orderly (Fast Tool) — know who to send it to. Repair agents: XM Repair Agents do this with RSSX or the XM Ops Tool. No access? Follow your normal escalation path. Eligible: The line was voluntarily canceled and meets the other criteria. Xfinity Internet is required. Most recently canceled lines can be brought back with Reactivate a line in XM360. Never eligible: These lines can't be reconnected under any circumstances: Line was ceased over 30 days ago and the number was returned to the original provider.; Mobile device number (MDN) has been ported out to another provider.; Fraud-related deactivations (must be handled by the Fraud team).; Lines in collections cease status (121+ days of non-payment).; Customers without active Xfinity Core or Mobile accounts.; Xfinity Mobile only customers with no active lines.; Customer is at their line limit and not eligible to activate another MDN.; Customer no longer has the device, or the device has been returned.

docs.title: By SIM type
docs.text: eSIM: Reconnect with RSSX or the XM Ops Tool. Try reconnecting the line using the Xfinity Mobile Network troubleshooting tool. If it says the ICCID is already in use, open an XM Support case in Enterprise Case Management (ECM). pSIM: Physical SIMs and eSIMs can both be reconnected with RSSX or the XM Ops Tool. CRM order fails: Reactivate in RSSX or XM Ops Tool, then complete the order. If the order fails in Customer Relationship Management (CRM), reactivate the line using RSSX or the XM Ops Tool. Then complete the order in CRM (for those with access) or Fast Tool/Orderly (for those without). This updates the line as active in XM360.

docs.title: Check for a pending order
docs.text: See whether a pending order is blocking changes to a line or account in XM360, and what kind of order it is. After activation, any change to the account or a line creates an order that goes from pending to completed. While an order is pending, no more changes can be made. Buttons and actions that aren't allowed are grayed out until the order completes. Refresh the screen to see the status. Once the order is completed, the options become active again. Common order types: Phone number changes.; Plan or feature changes.; IMEI or ICCID swaps.; Ceasing, resuming, or suspending service. Order types include but aren't limited to these.

docs.title: MBC codes — orders, carts and payments
crumbs: Look up an XM360 error code
MBC codes — orders, carts and payments
docs.text: Order, cart, payment, verification and system errors. We’re sorry, it looks like an error occurred while Invoking Payment Service-SubmitPayment. — There is an issue with the customer’s card. Try a different card or ask them to contact their bank.; We’re sorry, it looks like an error occurred while invoking Payment Service-AuthorizePayment. — Request a different card or other form of payment. The credit card has reached the limit. The customer must use a new card.; Not Authorized — The agent’s profile isn’t allowed to make this change. Escalate to a supervisor. The supervisor should request access for their agent. If the agent still does not have access, then their role doesn’t have the required permission. To assist the customer, follow the standard escalation steps.; An error occurred while canceling the order. — Follow the steps listed above this table.; We’re sorry, it looks like an error occurred while retrieving authorization token. — Xfinity Mobile has a transaction maximum of $5,000. docs.title: MSPAGENT codes — page and server
crumbs: Look up an XM360 error code
docs.text: The page or server didn't respond. Standard HTTP error response code, indicating the browser was able to communicate with the server, but the server could not find what was requested. — Refresh the page or wait a few minutes and try again. It’s likely an issue with the server and will be resolved automatically.; API failure error — Exit the session and retry. If the issue persists, follow the steps listed above.; Bad gateway. — This error appears when an action fails. Try using a different browser, clearing cache, using developer tools (press F12), or close the error and try again.; Server unavailable. — Refresh the page or wait a few minutes and try again. "Steps listed above" means the steps in When you get an error at the top of this guide.

crumbs: Look up an XM360 error code
NDEL codes — new device on an existing line
docs.text: The line or device isn't ready for an NDEL order. Line status is ineligible. — Advise the customer the line isn’t eligible for an early upgrade/NDEL.; Line status is ineligible. — Lines with a pending return (RMA) can’t be processed as an NDEL order.; Line has a pending activation request for NDEL. — Finish activating the NDEL device.; Line has reached maximum DPP allowed. — Confirm the customer is eligible for an additional line and follow the steps listed above this table.; Line status is Voluntary Suspended. — Confirm the customer qualifies to resume service and follow the steps listed above this table.; Device has open claims. — This device has an open claim with Assurant.; Device has open offers. — This device has an open trade-in offer with Assurant.; Device is not active on the line. — Confirm the IMEI and ICCID the customer is using and follow the steps listed above this table.; Line has a pending activation request for a held NDEL order. — Finish activating the NDEL device. "Steps listed above" means the steps in When you get an error at the top of this guide.

docs.text: Fix Xfinity Mobile eligibility problems caused by a username linked to the wrong or a disconnected account. Someone else's info: Customer sees someone else's account information. Not eligible: Einstein 360 shows an eligible customer as not eligible. Error or missing service: No Xfinity Mobile services show, or a "not the Primary user" error. Unlink extra accounts if issues continue. The linked account belongs to another customer.; The linked accounts are disconnected.; Errors continue, such as update payment errors. Fixing the default account fixes most issues. You'll also need to unlink the username from additional accounts when:

Old address after a move? Make sure CRM has the new account details. Follow the usual process so CRM has the correct new account number, AuthGUID and address. For updating an AuthGUID in RADAR, see assisting Mobile customers who recently moved.

crumbs: Troubleshoot an eSIM with Manage SIM Troubleshooting
docs.text: Use XM360's built-in SIM troubleshooting when an eSIM device isn't showing a green CN — Connected or CN — Installed Enabled status. XM360 shows each device's Network Status — use it to spot eSIM problems. RS: RS — device is ready to set up and connect to the network. CN: CN — device is connected to the network and active. Green: Green means ready (RS) or connected and working. Red: Red means there's a problem with the eSIM. When to use: Not showing green CN - Connected or CN - Installed Enabled? Use Manage SIM Troubleshooting. Also use it if the customer downloaded the eSIM but still needs help.

Follow the built-in steps; reissue an eSIM if the option shows. If there's no option to reissue an eSIM, the issue isn't SIM-related. Use Qelp or an Interactive Troubleshooting Guide (ITG) for the customer's issue to keep troubleshooting the device.

Always send SIM cards through XM360 with these steps. One SIM card ships per transaction. If more than one device needs a replacement pSIM, place a separate transaction for each device.

crumbs: Replace a physical SIM (pSIM) card in XM360
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: Authenticate the customer in Einstein 360. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.
Launch XM360.
Go to Devices.
Pick the device, then click Manage SIM Troubleshooting.

Pick a reason from the drop-down that matches the issue. Unable to make calls; Unable to send messages; Unable to use mobile data; Damaged SIM; Lost device; 4G to 5G swap; Switch SIM activation type. Any reason except Switch SIM activation type results in a pSIM replacement. For Switch SIM activation type, see Switch a pSIM to eSIM.

docs.title: Switch a pSIM to eSIM in XM360
crumbs: Switch a pSIM to eSIM in XM360
docs.text: Move a customer from a physical SIM to an eSIM on the same device. eSIM-to-pSIM switches aren't available. Only pSIM to eSIM is allowed — eSIM to pSIM isn't available. The device must support both SIM types and be eligible for eSIM activation. The pSIM option is greyed out on purpose when eSIM will work. When selling a device, pSIM is greyed out when we know the device will activate successfully with eSIM. eSIM is the safest and fastest way to connect to our network, adds no extra risk and makes setup smoother. Don't escalate eSIM-to-pSIM requests to ECM > XM Support. Heads up: Escalate only for a verified system error that blocks activation — never to override the eSIM-preferred flow. Front-line teams should proceed with the standard activation flow as presented.

crumbs: Switch a pSIM to eSIM in XM360
docs.text: 7 steps.

steps.text: Authenticate the customer in Einstein 360. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.
Launch XM360 and go to Devices.
Pick the device, then click Manage SIM Troubleshooting.
Choose Switch SIM activation type from the reason drop-down.
Confirm the switch from pSIM to eSIM, then click Continue. You'll see: A pop-up says SIM Switch in progress.
Have the customer download the eSIM once replacement is confirmed. XM360 requires the eSIM download after the eSIM replacement is confirmed.
Activate the customer's eSIM. See Activate a device in XM360.

docs.title: Activate a device in XM360
docs.text: Activate an eSIM or pSIM phone or tablet in XM360 — BYOD, new device on an existing line, or a replacement device. Encourage customers to activate in the Xfinity app first. They get activation instructions with their device. You can share the how to activate a phone article for easy steps. Same steps for BYOD, NDEL and replacement phones and tablets. Covers replacements through Xfinity Mobile Care (XMC), Apple or other manufacturers. Don't refer the customer to the manufacturer or Assurant. Doesn't apply to smartwatches — see how to activate a smartwatch. One mobile service per device, even on dual SIM phones. Xfinity Mobile, Comcast Business Mobile or NOW Mobile — only one per device. Dual SIM can still hold a second line from another domestic carrier or a local data plan when traveling abroad. These steps also apply to NOW Mobile customers. Recent port-ins can show in both Activations and Devices. Devices bought in the last 60 days with a pending number port show in both tabs until the port completes or 60 days pass. Don't activate an XMC replacement as a BYOD order. See Activate a replacement device in XM360.

docs.title: Activate the device
docs.text: 11 steps.

steps.text: Authenticate the customer using the method shown in Einstein 360. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.
Open XM360.
Select the Devices tab, then Activations.
Select the device to activate. Confirm the customer isn't currently using the device they want to activate.; Ask the customer to power off the device.
Complete ID proofing if prompted on an iPad in the store. A BYOD badge marks customer-owned devices.

Select New Number or Submit a Port. Heads up: Always collect an alternate contact number. When the port completes, the customer loses service with their old provider. Submit a Port keeps an existing phone number.

eSIM: have the customer set up the phone so the eSIM downloads. Turn on the device and follow the on-screen steps.; Connect to a WiFi network.; Keep following the steps to the home screen — the eSIM downloads and activates.; Check for cellular bars in the upper right corner. The eSIM should download automatically during first-time setup. pSIM devices skip to inserting the SIM.

eSIM download failed? Use the fallback options. Have the customer check for a push notification from the Xfinity app.; Check the phone settings.; Send the customer a QR code. Open the Camera app. Scan the QR code. Follow the on-screen prompts.; Still stuck? They can enter a URL on the device to download the eSIM — see Manually enter a URL in how to activate a phone with Xfinity Mobile or NOW Mobile. Tip: The QR code is in the email inbox linked to the customer's account. If they can't scan it, get a manual code from the eSIM activation guide.
Select Continue once the eSIM downloads or the pSIM is in. For a pSIM, answer the question asking if the SIM card was inserted correctly.

Verify the device works on the network. Have the customer power the device off and back on.; Confirm the carrier shows as Xfinity Mobile in the status bar.; Send a text or make a call while off WiFi.; Install the Xfinity app.
All good? Select Yes: All the steps above were successful, then Finish. If anything failed, select No: Some steps weren't successful.
