docs.title: Xfinity Retail Store messages
docs.text: What the verification messages mean and what to do. "Verification status not started. Customer must go into the Xfinity app to complete process.". The customer hasn't tried activating in the Xfinity app. They must attempt activation and get an unsuccessful message in the app before you can help. "Verification complete. Customer must go into the Xfinity app to complete process.". The customer didn't finish activating in the Xfinity app. They must attempt activation and get an unsuccessful message in the app before you can help. "No seasoned contact at this time. Customer must go into a store to complete process.". No seasoned contact method is on file. They must visit an Xfinity Retail Store to complete ID proofing, including a knowledge-based question, to finish activation. "No seasoned contact at this time. Please use iPad to complete process.". No seasoned contact method is on file. Complete ID proofing, including a knowledge-based question, before completing activation. "Verification status not started / pending / complete. Please use iPad or have the customer use the Xfinity app to complete process.". Encourage the customer to activate in the Xfinity app. If needed, use the iPad to complete ID proofing, including a knowledge-based question, before completing activation.

docs.title: Activate a replacement device in XM360
crumbs: Activate a replacement device in XM360
docs.text: Enter a new IMEI and activate an insurance or manufacturer (OEM) replacement phone when it doesn't show as ready to activate. Retail reps can activate replacement devices in XM360. Use these steps for XMC, Apple and other manufacturer replacements. Don't refer the customer to the manufacturer or Assurant. Don't activate an XMC replacement as a BYOD order on a new or existing line. Customer authorization through Step Up is required to update an IMEI. No Activate button? The new IMEI likely hasn't reached Comcast yet. The replacement IMEI from Assurant or the OEM can be delayed. Enter the new IMEI in XM360 and activate the phone right away. When the IMEI file arrives, Comcast updates the biller so the new IMEI is active on the biller and network.

docs.title: Enter the replacement IMEI
crumbs: Activate a replacement device in XM360
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: Open the device in XM360 and select Activate Replacement Device. Where: Device Details page, in Actions. Heads up: Don't use this for BYO devices — use Replace with eSIM BYOD or Replace with no-SIM BYOD instead. Confirm it's a verified insurance or OEM replacement first. For the start of the flow, see Activate a device in XM360.
Choose insurance or OEM replacement, enter IMEI 1, then Continue. Heads up: Enter IMEI 1, not IMEI 2 — Assurant only sends Comcast IMEI 1.
Wait for the IMEI update — it can take up to 5 minutes. You'll see: The customer gets an email: "We have received your request to activate a replacement device.".
Watch for the "device is active" email. You'll see: The customer gets a second email once the device is active on the network.
Finish the activation steps. Download the eSIM or insert the pSIM, select Continue, and verify the device on the network. See Activate a device in XM360.

docs.text: Confirm (or reject) a new IMEI as an insurance or OEM replacement so features and promotions move to the new device. Only agents with the right permissions. They can confirm non-Apple OEM devices right away, and insurance replacements not auto-verified after 72 hours. XM Support agents see an overlay with Verify replacement device or Not a replacement device (BYO).

docs.title: Verify the device
docs.text: 4 steps.

steps.text: Pick Verify replacement device or Not a replacement device.
Verify replacement device moves insurance, features and promos to the new IMEI. You'll see: Device Details shows only the new IMEI.

Use Not a replacement device if it isn't one and the old IMEI owes DPP. You'll see: The customer gets an email saying the device wasn't confirmed as a replacement. They can still use the new device on the network.

Expect "Different device is active on the network" with an Align button. Tip: If the customer has XMC on the old device they aren't using, ask if they want to cancel insurance on the IMEI active in the biller. This is an acceptable state — no changes needed unless the customer wants to pay off the old device and buy insurance for the one they're using. Align walks you through paying off the original device. See Align IMEIs in XM360.

docs.title: Align IMEIs in XM360
docs.text: Match the biller IMEI to the network IMEI when they differ and the customer needs an order that requires them to match. Normally the network and biller show the same single IMEI. A mismatch shows Different IMEI is active on the network and an Align button. Both the Biller and Network IMEI appear. Causes: activation errors, an unsolicited SIM swap by the customer, or a BYOD activated without paying off the original device. Never use Align to fix network connectivity. Heads up: Aligning won't help connectivity. Use it only when the IMEI is connected to the network and the customer needs an order that requires the Biller IMEI to match the Network IMEI. Retail and Care can use Align; Step Up authorization is required. Customer authorization through Step Up is required to update an IMEI. Customer may choose not to align. For example, if they want to keep paying for their DPP device while using a BYOD phone on the network.
keywords: different imei active on the network

docs.title: Two types of mismatch
docs.text: Two devices: Two phones on one line (MDN): old IMEI in billing, new one on network. Buy Xfinity Mobile Care (XMC) for the device active on the network; MDN swap; Line transfer; Pair watch; Service change. Example: a BYOD customer activates a new phone while still paying off an old device on DPP. After the old phone is paid off, Align updates billing to the phone they use now. Agents without permission must escalate via Enterprise Case Management (ECM) Chat. Aligning is needed for these actions to work without errors: Same device: One phone with IMEI 1 in the biller and IMEI 2 on the network. MDN swap; Line transfer; Pair watch. Usually from activating on the alternate IMEI after an error — Verizon errors R751, R625 and R140 are common triggers. Activate on IMEI 2, then use Align to match the biller. Needed for these actions to work without errors:

docs.title: Troubleshoot eSIM activation
docs.text: Help customers through eSIM activation problems — best practices, checking the download, a missing eSIM, and what never to do. eSIM is normal and secure. It's the safest and fastest way to connect to the Xfinity network, adds no extra risk and makes setup easier. Activation can take a few minutes while steps finish in the background. Activations typically take less than 10 minutes. Use only approved troubleshooting steps. Heads up: Improper workarounds can make a customer lose their phone number and need more support.

docs.title: Who handles what
docs.text: New line activation — ✓ — ✓ — ✓; Bring your own device (BYOD) activation — ✓ — ✓ — ✓; New device existing line (NDEL) activation — ✓ — ✓ — ✓; Early upgrades — ✓ — ✓ — ✓; Bring your own new device on an existing line (BYONDEL) — ✓ — ✓ — ✓; eSIM replacement — ✓ — ✓ — ✓; Moving from eSIM to pSIM or pSIM to eSIM on the same device — ✓ pSIM to eSIM only. eSIM to pSIM isn't available — don't escalate those requests to ECM > XM Support. — ✓ — ✗. XMC = Xfinity Mobile Care Center of Excellence (CoE). For switching SIMs, see Switch a pSIM to eSIM.

docs.title: Devices activated by eSIM
docs.text: BYOD: Always check the device in the BYOD IMEI Lookup tool. Enter an IMEI to check eSIM and network compatibility. For more, see Xfinity Mobile BYOD overview. Unlocked: BYOD devices must be unlocked. If the lock status can't be determined, the customer can't request an eSIM or a pSIM card shipment. eSIM logic: pSIM is greyed out when the buyflow picks eSIM. This means faster activation — no waiting for a pSIM, and eSIM devices activate within minutes. One-time PIN: NDEL and BYONDEL need one-time PIN verification. pSIM users can move the SIM card from the old device to the new one, but still need one-time PIN verification. eSIM users need it too. Both follow the Activating a device on an existing line section of how to activate a phone or tablet with Xfinity Mobile and NOW Mobile. Watches: All smartwatches activate with eSIM and have only one IMEI. New line: NDNL or BYODNDNL: device is ready — follow the on-screen setup. "Great news! Your device is ready to connect. Just follow the on screen instructions to complete the setup.". Existing line: NDEL or BYONDEL: start activation from the Xfinity app. Use the app on the device being activated or on another device with the Xfinity app installed.

docs.title: Before trying again (multi-SIM devices)
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: Not bought from Xfinity Mobile? Make sure it's unlocked. See how to unlock the phone I'm bringing from my carrier.
Connect to working WiFi. Tip: Best practice: always connect to WiFi before starting any activation.
Remove the pSIM card if they aren't using it.
Update the device software to the latest version.
Restart the device and try again.

docs.text: 3 steps.

steps.text: Check Network status on the device's detail page in XM360. You'll see: CN — Connected or CN — Installed Enabled means the eSIM downloaded and should work.
Have the customer test a call or app download with WiFi off.

Still needs help? Use Manage SIM Troubleshooting. Also use it if the status isn't CN — Connected or CN — Installed Enabled. See Troubleshoot an eSIM with Manage SIM Troubleshooting. Customers who want to do it themselves can use what to do if an eSIM or nanoSIM isn't working.

docs.text: eSIM install should finish within 10 minutes. Deleted or missing eSIM? Use Manage SIM Troubleshooting to send a new one. See Troubleshoot an eSIM with Manage SIM Troubleshooting. Don't do SIM swaps or line deactivations on a device with no eSIM. If you've done all the troubleshooting and service still isn't restored, escalate using standard procedures.

docs.title: Swapping between pSIM and eSIM devices
crumbs: Swapping between pSIM and eSIM devices
docs.text: Moving a line from a pSIM device to an eSIM device (or back) can cause activation errors and lose the phone number. Only correct process: early upgrade or NDEL with eSIM, or Replace with an eSIM BYOD device. Don't use these to fix an eSIM activation: Submit a "provide order" for the eSIM device.; Activate the device with a new phone number.; Attempt a Pair SIM order.; Deactivate and reactivate the line. Heads up: These cause device status issues and may lose the customer's phone number. Phone number lost? Create a ticket to help recover it.
keywords: swapping between psim and esim devices

docs.title: Fix eSIM activation error messages
docs.text: What to do when the buy flow shows a timeout, IMEI eligibility error, or carrier-locked message during eSIM activation. Retry the activation up to two more times. If the error keeps showing, the device can't activate on the Xfinity Mobile network with an eSIM.

docs.title: Timeout (system error)
docs.text: Eligibility API issue: 404s, 500, timeouts, and false eligibility. 2 steps.

steps.text: Select Retry to see if it clears.
After three retries, the pop-up closes and an error shows on the IMEI checker. You'll see: Red banner: "BYOD check has reached the maximum number of retries. Please try again.".

Carrier locked — Hard stop: the order can't continue. Banner text: "this device is currently locked by its carrier, and this order cannot continue. Please review article for further steps.".

Carrier may be locked — Soft stop: the device may be locked. Banner text: "this device may be locked. If this device is locked, the device cannot be activated. Please view article for further steps.".

Locked device? Share "How do I unlock the phone I'm bringing from my carrier?". Tip: Apple users must back up and factory reset after their old provider confirms the unlock. See Factory reset without losing the eSIM or the Apple Support article. A locked device can't be activated with Xfinity Mobile.

docs.title: Fix an iPhone stuck in SOS mode
crumbs: Fix an iPhone stuck in SOS mode
docs.text: Get an Apple device out of SOS mode when the eSIM wasn't downloaded before activation. Some iPhones go to SOS if the eSIM isn't downloaded before activation. "SOS" shows in the status bar, upper right. In SOS mode, customers can only place emergency calls.

docs.title: Get out of SOS mode
crumbs: Fix an iPhone stuck in SOS mode
docs.text: After eSIM activation, customers still see SOS in no-coverage areas, as normal. 7 steps.

steps.text: Verify the customer has an eSIM installed. Heads up: The next steps won't fix it unless an eSIM is installed.
Check for the Carrier Cellular Plan Ready to Be Installed notification. Customers activating a new iPhone 13, 14 or SE (third generation) should have received it.
Have them go to Settings and tap Carrier Cellular Plan Ready to Be Installed.
Tap Continue at the bottom of the screen. You'll see: The eSIM should download and install.
Toggle airplane mode on, wait at least 15 seconds, then off. Where: Settings > Turn on Airplane Mode > Turn off Airplane Mode.
Still SOS? Reset network settings. Where: Settings > General > Transfer or Reset Device > Reset > Reset Network Settings. You'll see: The phone should reset within about five minutes.
Didn't work the first time? Repeat the steps. In most cases the reset and restart forces the phone out of SOS mode. You can also share Apple's help page.

docs.title: Factory reset without losing the eSIM
crumbs: Factory reset without losing the eSIM
docs.text: When a factory reset is part of troubleshooting, make sure the customer keeps their eSIM so they don't lose network access. The customer must choose to keep their eSIM during the reset. Heads up: Erasing the eSIM removes access to the Xfinity Mobile network.

docs.title: Apple devices
crumbs: Factory reset without losing the eSIM
docs.text: 3 steps.

steps.text: Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset > Erase All Content and Settings.
Enter the passcode or Apple Account password.
Choose to keep the eSIM. The customer can choose to erase their eSIM or keep it.

docs.title: Google Pixel devices
crumbs: Factory reset without losing the eSIM
docs.text: 2 steps.

steps.text: Go to Settings > System > Reset Options > Erase all data (factory reset).
Choose to keep the eSIM. The customer can choose to erase their eSIM or keep it.

docs.title: Samsung devices
crumbs: Factory reset without losing the eSIM
docs.text: 2 steps.

steps.text: Go to Settings > General management > Reset > Factory data reset > Reset.
Choose to keep the eSIM. The customer can choose to erase their eSIM or keep it.

docs.title: Delete an eSIM from a device
crumbs: Delete an eSIM from a device
docs.text: Remove an old eSIM from an iPhone, Samsung, Motorola or Pixel before a SIM replacement, so the line keeps service. Skipping this shows SIM Transferred after the replacement eSIM activates. If the member isn't told to remove an existing eSIM before you use the replace SIM function, XM360's device page shows "SIM Transferred" after the replacement eSIM activates. A second eSIM replacement leaves the device with no service. Heads up: If a second eSIM replacement is started, the device will no longer have service. Deleting an eSIM doesn't cancel the cellular plan. Erase all content and settings? The member can keep or erase the eSIM. See Factory reset without losing the eSIM. For more device help, see the Device Support page on xfinity.com/mobile.

docs.title: Apple (iPhone and iPad)
crumbs: Delete an eSIM from a device
docs.text: Only for iPhone and iPad models that support eSIM. More: Apple's Remove an eSIM article. 4 steps.

steps.text: Open Settings.
Select Cellular, then the plan to erase.
Select Delete eSIM.
Select Delete eSIM again to confirm.

docs.title: Samsung
crumbs: Delete an eSIM from a device
docs.text: Only for Samsung devices that support eSIM. More: Samsung's Remove an eSIM article. 4 steps.

steps.text: Open Settings.
Select Connections, then SIM card manager.
Select the eSIM, then Remove.
Confirm Remove the eSIM.

docs.title: Motorola
crumbs: Delete an eSIM from a device
docs.text: Only for Motorola devices that support eSIM. More: Motorola's Remove an eSIM article. 4 steps.

steps.text: Open Settings.
Select Connected devices, then Mobile data.
Select the eSIM, then Erase SIM.
Confirm Erase the eSIM.

docs.title: Google Pixel
crumbs: Delete an eSIM from a device
docs.text: Only for Google Pixel devices that support eSIM. More: Google's Remove an eSIM article. 4 steps.

steps.text: Open Settings.
Select Network and Internet, then SIMs.
Choose the eSIM, then Erase SIM.
Confirm Erase the eSIM.

docs.title: Fix a physical SIM that isn't working
crumbs: Fix a physical SIM that isn't working
docs.text: Clean and reseat a pSIM, spot ineligible devices, and handle known defective SIM cards when a phone shows No SIM or SOS. A SIM problem can show as any of these. The pSIM may just need reseating or cleaning; an eSIM may have been deleted by accident. "No SIM.". "Insert SIM card.". "SOS.". eSIM deleted? See Recover a deleted eSIM.

docs.title: Check and clean the pSIM
crumbs: Fix a physical SIM that isn't working
docs.text: Still not working after cleaning? It may be a third-party manufacturer issue — Xfinity can help figure it out and replace the SIM card if needed. See Replace a physical SIM (pSIM) card in XM360. 8 steps.

steps.text: Turn off the phone.
Pop the SIM tray with a SIM ejector tool or paperclip.
Remove the pSIM card. To find the tray, see support for the device: Samsung phone, Apple iPhone, Pixel phone or Motorola phone.
Look for dust or dirt on the gold contacts.
Gently clean the gold contacts with a soft cloth.
Put the pSIM back in the tray, chip facing down.
Insert the tray into the phone.
Restart the phone.

docs.title: Moved the SIM to another phone?
crumbs: Fix a physical SIM that isn't working
Moved the SIM to another phone?
docs.text: If calls stopped after moving the pSIM to a new device, the device may not be allowed on the Xfinity network. The device was reported lost or stolen. The device was meant for Prepaid service. The device has an outstanding balance with the previous provider. The device isn't certified for use on our network. If the device fits one of these, service is suspended briefly.
keywords: moved the sim to another phone?

docs.title: Known defective pSIM cards
crumbs: Fix a physical SIM that isn't working
docs.text: A pSIM manufacturer's mistake can cause "No Service" or "SOS". It's not an issue with Xfinity Mobile products or services, and the cards won't damage devices. 4 steps.

steps.text: Encourage switching to eSIM if the phone supports it. Otherwise, just swap the pSIM card for a new one. See Switch a pSIM to eSIM.

Swapping a card? Enter the new card's ICCID. Stores may have bad cards in stock. If you enter the 16-digit Integrated Circuit Card ID (ICCID) and it's bad, you'll see Error - Defective SIM: "Please enter a different SIM and dispose of current one.".
Pulled a defective card? Try another card. No need to keep bad cards — dispose of them as you normally would.
Swap didn't fix it? Troubleshoot and escalate as needed. See Manage SIM in XM360 and the SIM swap policy. Care agents send a new card following the SIM swap policy.

docs.title: Einstein Smart Message
crumbs: Fix a physical SIM that isn't working
docs.text: Affected customers were emailed and have a Smart Message on their account. This customer may need to replace their pSIM card — "A bad physical SIM (pSIM) card may be affecting this customer's mobile service. Help them replace their pSIM card and / or encourage them to activate an eSIM card (if their device is eSIM capable).".

docs.title: Recover a deleted eSIM
docs.text: Help a customer download a new eSIM after deleting theirs by accident — online, in the Xfinity app, by QR code or by URL. A deleted eSIM means no network access until a new one downloads. The device must be in RS (Ready State) first. The customer must be in RS before they can get a push notification to activate. In RS they can also activate with a QR code. To check eSIM status or fix activation issues, see Troubleshoot an eSIM with Manage SIM Troubleshooting.

docs.title: Option 1: Xfinity Mobile account online
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: Sign in online with the Primary or Manager's Xfinity ID.
Select Devices, then the device to update.
Under eSIM download and help, click eSIM details. Where: On the Device's Details page.
Select Get a new eSIM.
Select Add SIM and follow the prompts. Or download it manually by scanning the QR Code or choosing enter a code manually.

docs.title: Option 2: Xfinity app
docs.text: 7 steps.

steps.text: Open the Xfinity app and sign in with the Primary or Manager's Xfinity ID.
On Services, tap Mobile lines and data usage. Where: Inside the Mobile services card.
Select the phone line, then tap the device.
Under Device Management, tap Download a new eSIM. They may need to sign in again.
Select Get a new eSIM.
Select Add SIM and follow the prompts. Or download it manually by scanning the QR Code or choosing enter a code manually.
Toggle the eSIM on if needed. Google & Motorola: Settings > Network & Internet > SIMs; Samsung: Settings > Connections > SIM Manager.

docs.title: Option 3: QR code
docs.text: 1 steps.

steps.text: eSIM didn't download? Scan this QR code and follow the prompts.

media.alt: QR code customers scan to follow the on-screen prompts and download an eSIM.
media.caption: Scan to download the eSIM

docs.title: Option 4: Enter a URL manually
docs.text: If the eSIM still won't download, enter the address on the device. Apple — Open Settings > Cellular or Mobile Data > Add Cellular Plan (or Add eSIM and use QR code) > Enter Details Manually. Enter cct.vzw.otgeuicc.com in SM-DP+ Address. Leave Activation Code and Confirmation Code blank. Select Next and follow the steps.; Samsung Galaxy — Open Settings > Connections > SIM manager > Add eSIM > Scan QR code. When prompted, select Enter Activation code, enter LPA:1$cct.vzw.otgeuicc.com, then Done.; Google Pixel — Network & Internet > SIMs > Add SIM > Download a SIM Instead (select Use a different network if Xfinity Mobile isn't listed). On Scan QR code, select Need help? > Enter it manually. Enter LPA:1$cct.vzw.otgeuicc.com$, then Continue.; Motorola — Open Settings > Network & Internet > Mobile Network or SIMs & mobile network > Add SIM (or +) > Enter code manually. Enter LPA:1$cct.vzw.otgeuicc.com$, then Done.

docs.title: More help for the customer
docs.text: Point them to the Xfinity app for self-service support. The app is the easiest way to activate, manage and troubleshoot, with 24/7 support, bill pay, plan details and outage updates. They can scan this QR code to get it, visit the Online Support Center, or ask Xfinity Assistant.

docs.title: Turn the SIM PIN on or off
crumbs: Turn the SIM PIN on or off
docs.text: Turn a phone's SIM PIN lock on or off, or change it, on Apple, Samsung, Motorola, LG and Google phones. A SIM PIN is a four- to eight-digit passcode that locks the SIM to the device. When a SIM PIN and another security feature (like a lock screen passcode or Face ID) are both on, the SIM PIN must be entered first. The default SIM PIN is 1111. If the device has never used a SIM PIN, enter 1111. 10 wrong SIM PIN tries locks the device until a PUK code is entered. Heads up: Don't let the customer keep guessing. After 10 wrong tries they'll need a Personal Unlock Key (PUK). The PUK code is tied to the SIM card's ICCID. See Get a PUK code.

docs.title: Apple devices
crumbs: Turn the SIM PIN on or off
docs.text: 6 steps.

steps.text: Go to Settings.
Tap Cellular, then SIM PIN.
Turn SIM PIN on or off.
If asked, enter the SIM PIN — the default is 1111. If 1111 doesn't work, follow the PUK code steps to get SIM PIN 2. See Get a PUK code.
Tap Done.
To change it from 1111, tap Change PIN. Tip: Only if the customer wants a PIN other than the default.

docs.title: Samsung devices
crumbs: Turn the SIM PIN on or off
docs.text: 8 steps.

steps.text: From the home screen, swipe up to see all apps.
Go to Settings, then Security and privacy.
Tap More Security Settings, then SIM card security.
Turn Lock SIM card on or off.
Tap Change SIM card PIN.
Enter 1111, the default SIM PIN. If 1111 doesn't work, follow the PUK code steps to get SIM PIN 2. See Get a PUK code.
Enter a new SIM PIN and tap OK.
Enter the new SIM PIN again and tap OK.

docs.title: Motorola devices
crumbs: Turn the SIM PIN on or off
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: From the Home screen, swipe up from the center to open apps.
Go to Settings, then Security & Location.
In the SIM card lock section, pick the phone number.
Tap Lock SIM card to turn it on or off.
Enter the SIM PIN and tap OK — default is 1111. If 1111 doesn't work, follow the PUK code steps to get SIM PIN 2. See Get a PUK code.

docs.title: LG devices
crumbs: Turn the SIM PIN on or off
docs.text: 4 steps.

steps.text: From the Home screen, go to Settings, then Lock screen & security.
Tap Set up SIM card lock.
Tap Lock SIM card to turn it on or off.
Enter the current SIM PIN and tap OK — default is 1111. If 1111 doesn't work, follow the PUK code steps to get SIM PIN 2. See Get a PUK code.

docs.title: Google devices
crumbs: Turn the SIM PIN on or off
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: From the Home screen, swipe up to show all apps.
Go to Settings, then Security.
Tap SIM card lock.
Tap Lock SIM card to turn it on or off.
Enter the SIM PIN and tap OK — default is 1111. If 1111 doesn't work, follow the PUK code steps to get SIM PIN 2. See Get a PUK code.

docs.title: Get a PUK code for a locked SIM
crumbs: Get a PUK code for a locked SIM
Check what the phone is asking for
docs.text: Look up the PUK code (and SIM PIN 2) in XiSCO when a phone is asking for a PUK after too many wrong SIM PINs. 2 steps.
keywords: check what the phone is asking for

steps.text: Confirm the phone screen is asking for a PUK code. If they really want to unlock the phone to use another provider's SIM, see Unlock a phone in XM360.; If it shows Please enter your SIM PIN instead, enter the default 1111 (if the customer never changed it).
If 1111 doesn't work, look up PIN 2 and try it first. Have the customer try PIN 2 before you move on to the PUK code.

docs.title: Look up the PUK code
crumbs: Get a PUK code for a locked SIM
docs.text: The PUK code matches the SIM card's ICCID and is created by the Xfinity Mobile Data Visualization (XMDV) tool. 5 steps.

steps.text: Open the New Warehouse Tracker to get to XiSCO.
Click PIN/PUK Codes in the General section.
Enter the SIM's ICCID and click Search. Need the ICCID? See Find a device's IMEI and ICCID.
Give the customer the first PUK code. You'll see: You'll see two PIN codes and two PUK codes. If the first set doesn't work, give them the second set to try.
After the PUK, enter the SIM PIN twice to get into the device. You'll see: Once the PUK code is entered, the device switches back to asking for the SIM PIN.

media.alt: New Warehouse Tracker General section listing Collections, Condor, Customer Moves, ILD Roaming Rates and PIN PUK Codes.
media.caption: PIN/PUK Codes link in the General section

media.alt: XiSCO PIN PUK Codes search box labeled Enter ICCID, with Clear and Search buttons.
media.caption: Search by ICCID

docs.title: If the PUK doesn't work
crumbs: Get a PUK code for a locked SIM
docs.text: Replace the SIM card if the PUK fails or the SIM PIN still won't take. If the PUK code doesn't remove the PUK lock, or it worked but the customer still can't enter the correct SIM PIN, the customer needs a new SIM card. Manage the SIM change in XM360.

docs.title: Reset a phone's network settings
docs.text: When and how to have a customer reset network settings so the phone picks up its line, number or SIM change. The phone was set up before the line was activated. Encourage customers to leave a new device powered off until it's activated. Some turn it on, set it up and restore data from the old device before the new one is active. A SIM update was done in XM360. You'll see: Resetting network settings and restarting makes the new device (IMEI) show in the RSSX/XM Network Troubleshooting Tool and XM360. For example, they moved the pSIM (physical SIM) from one device to another. That updates the SIM in the RSSX/XM Network Troubleshooting Tool. The line was deactivated and reactivated in CRM or the network tool. CRM and/or the RSSX/XM Network Troubleshooting Tool. The phone number (MDN) was changed in XM360 or CRM. Any mobile device number change — new number to new number, new number to ported number, etc. There are known LTE issues a reset can fix. Only do this if: The IMEI and ICCID are correct in XM360, CRM and the RSSX/XM Network Troubleshooting Tool. The customer has network coverage. The Access Point Name (APN) settings and cellular data option are right. In the RSSX/XM Network Troubleshooting Tool, the 4G/SIM status shows one of: RS: Pending SIM Over the air (OTA) Provisioning; RF: SIM OTA Provisioning has failed; CN: SIM OTA Provisioning is complete. Resetting network settings and restarting downloads the Xfinity Mobile carrier profile again.

docs.title: Reset the network settings
docs.text: 3 steps.

steps.text: Tell the customer saved network data will be erased. Heads up: Saved WiFi networks and passwords, Bluetooth pairings and similar settings are wiped. They'll need to re-enter them.
Look up the phone model on the Device Support page for exact steps. Steps differ by phone, so search the model there.
Reset network settings, then restart the phone.

docs.title: Check the line history
docs.text: 2 steps.

steps.text: In the XM Network Troubleshooting Tool, open Actions in Line information.
Select Line History.

docs.title: Reading the 4G status
docs.text: Suspend + restore can show CN even when OTA isn't really done. When the 4G status is RS (pending SIM OTA Provisioning), suspending and reactivating the line in CRM changes it to Core Network (CN) and the screen reads "SIM OTA Provisioning is complete." That doesn't actually mean SIM OTA Provisioning is complete. A suspended working line stays CN when restored. The tool automatically changes the 4G status to CN. Suspending and reactivating doesn't send the status back to RS the way deactivating and reactivating does. The tool knows when a device is reactivated after being suspended or hotlined and keeps it at CN so the customer can use the device — which can be misleading. Never suspend or hotline a line just to restore it during activation. Heads up: Activation steps should never include a suspend/hotline of the customer's line just to be restored.

docs.title: Fix a porting error in XM360
crumbs: Fix a porting error in XM360
docs.text: Open the port details in XM360, read the yellow or red error banner, fix it using the error-code table and resubmit the port. Make sure you're activating the correct line and device. Start the activation as an existing (ported) number. Wireless ports are due in 3 hours; wireline in 72 hours.

docs.title: Open the port details
crumbs: Fix a porting error in XM360
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: Find the customer's account and launch XM360. The article says to authenticate the customer in Einstein 360. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.
Go to Devices, then select Activations.
Find Resolution required and select See details.
Select Continue to open the Porting and Activation page. You'll see: This is where you fix the issue and resubmit the port.

Read the port status and the error banner. Porting status: current status of the port.; Submission date: when the port was entered.; Due date: when the port should complete. Wireless: 3 hours. Wireline: 72 hours.; Response details: error code details.; Yellow banners: errors you can fix.; Red banners: errors that need escalation (clickable links provided). Tip: Some roles can edit the due date for special cases or holidays/weekends. They can't pick a date earlier than the one shown — choose a future date from the drop-down and resubmit.

docs.title: Fix and resubmit
crumbs: Fix a porting error in XM360
docs.text: Don't cancel: Don't cancel the port request unless the error message tells you to. Follow the steps in the message to fix it and resubmit. 3 steps.

steps.text: Yellow banner: fix the info and resubmit the port. Common fixes: remove port protection, or correct the port info to match the previous service provider. Then resubmit.
Red banner: click the link to open an XM Support case. The link opens an XM Support case in Enterprise Case Management (ECM).
Match the error code in the table below and follow its action. Error reason codes (XM360) and R-codes (MySyniverse/Customer Relationship Management (CRM)) show in the expanded message banner.

docs.title: Error codes
crumbs: Fix a porting error in XM360
docs.text: 6B — R615, R616, R621, R622, R623, R659 — Port protection or PIN on account — Customer contacts their provider to remove port protection or get their PIN (see where to find the account info from the previous carrier). Resubmit the port.; 6P, 8C — R671, R680 — Transfer PIN/password needed or mismatch — Customer must get the correct PIN (see where to find the account info from the previous carrier). Enter the PIN in XM360. Resubmit the port.; 8A — R678 — Account number is incorrect — Customer contacts the previous provider for the correct account number. Resubmit the port.; 1L, 6F, 1N, 1M, 6E — R654, R663, R656, R655, R662 — Requested due date/time cannot be met — Change the due date. Resubmit the port. For porting intervals, check FetchItUp. Don't cancel the port.; 1P, 1P Other, 6C — R617, R618, R619, R620, R657, R660 — Read Remarks field for next steps — Confirm information and fix any mistakes. Ask the customer to contact their provider for missing information. Resubmit the port.; 6A, 6D — R658, R661 — Mobile device number (MDN) not found — Confirm the MDN; fix mistakes and resubmit if needed. Call the MDN to check if it's active. Not active: customer can contact the provider to reactivate, port a different number, or get a new Xfinity Mobile number. Active: check the Service Provider ID (SPID) in Neustar Port PS — if correct, customer contacts the provider; if incorrect, escalate.; E2201 — R220 — MDN already active on the account — Confirm the MDN. Fix mistakes and resubmit. If the MDN is correct and it continues, escalate.; E1029, E2243 — R601, R613 — Ported number…

Only cancel ports in XM360 — never in the XM Network Troubleshooting Tool. Heads up: Cancelling anywhere else causes activation delays. Only cancel if the error message tells you to. Otherwise fix the error and resubmit. See Fix a porting error in XM360.

docs.title: Build a manual port-in request
crumbs: When a manual port is needed
docs.text: The checklist to complete before you submit or rebuild an Xfinity Mobile port-in request by hand in MySyniverse. The OCN SPID in RSSX doesn't match the NPAC SPID in Neustar Port PS. This sends the port request to the wrong service provider. The port was put on hold, canceled, or the old provider couldn't process it. The old service provider (OSP) must explain why Xfinity Mobile should cancel the current request and submit a new one.; Always ask the OSP to escalate within their team first, before canceling a port request in MySyniverse. A wireline port was sent with the wrong Desired Due Date/Time. Rather than waiting up to 48 hours for the OSP to reject it, Xfinity Mobile cancels the request in MySyniverse and resubmits it.
keywords: when a manual port is needed

docs.title: Clear pending ports first
docs.text: 1 steps.

steps.text: Make sure there are no pending port-in orders. If there is one, cancel it before creating a new one. This prevents a Duplicate Port Request error.

docs.title: Complete the checklist
docs.text: Check every item before you submit or rebuild the request. 9 steps.

steps.text: Old Network: Match Old Network to the NPAC SPID in Neustar Port PS.
Group No.: Copy Group No. from the most recent request submitted.
Auto-activate: Set Auto-activate to Y.

Port Direction: Set Port Direction to Wireless to Wireless or Wireline to Wireless. It defaults to Wireless to Wireless. Only change to Wireline to Wireless if the customer is porting from a landline carrier (e.g., Xfinity Voice).

Due date: Set Desired Due D/T to three hours for a wireless port. Wireline ports can take two to 10 business days.; If the OSP says the port is complex, schedule it for seven business days and leave a Remark: "Please process as a complex port.".
Contacts: Fill in the creator and contact fields. Request Creator: RSS-ETNI Bridge; New SP Contact: LNP CENTER; Contact TN: 1-844-963-0117.

LRN: Use the LRN from RSSX — never the one from Neustar. Access RSSX. (No RSSX access? The XM network tool can be used — it automatically validates the MDN. Provide the MDN and show the LRN.); Select Tools.; Select Port-in Validation.; Enter the MDN and select Validate. Heads up: Don't use the LRN from Neustar Port PS — that's the current provider's LRN. A manual request needs the Xfinity Mobile local routing number, found only in RSSX. If the LRN is 0000000000 in RSSX, select Y.

Port to Original: Set Port to Original to N when RSSX shows a valid LRN. N — valid LRN in RSSX (e.g., 6019209998).; Y — the LRN is 0000000000 in RSSX.; D — the MDN is internal from 6006 to 6006 in RSSX.

Agency Auth: Complete Agency Authorization date and name. Date must be the same day the port request is sent.; Name must be the authorized user's name if the customer is moving a business number.; To see if an Agency Name is required, look up the SPID in Fetch it Up (for example, SPID 505B always requires an Auth name).

docs.title: Handle a delayed port request
docs.text: What to do when a port-in shows a Delay response type in MySyniverse — timing, checking Remarks, and calling the old provider. Wireless ports take eight minutes to three hours. Landline to mobile can take two to five business days. XM360 may show Port Processing on the Devices tab. The message reads "Port Processing. This might take a few minutes" after the port is submitted. You may see Activation Pending under MDN. Escalate a mobile port that takes longer than three hours. The status of a delayed port request should show in MySyniverse almost right away. If a mobile port takes longer than three hours, the Retail Representative or Xfinity Mobile Specialist should escalate. Landline ports: wait 24 hours for the provider to respond. If there's no response after 24 hours, escalate as needed.; Landline providers don't always respond within 24 hours.; Some wait until the due date selected on submission before responding.; If there's still no response by the due date, escalate.

docs.title: Work the delayed port
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: In MySyniverse, check Port Response for Response Type Delay. A Delay response type means the customer's current provider sent that response. It also includes a 6G — Port Complexity error message.
Open the PON and read the REMARKS area. Landline providers add notes about the delay here.

Not done in 12 minutes? Three-way call the old provider and customer. Find wireless provider contact info in the wireless carrier guide, or the Contact TN field under Port Response in MySyniverse.; The Contact TN number might belong to MySyniverse, not the service provider. Escalate the issue and contact the Old Service Provider (OSP) with the customer to complete or reject the port request.
If the info is right, the OSP sends a Confirm response. You'll see: Wait eight to 12 minutes for the number to become active in XM360.
If info is wrong, the OSP sends Resolution Required — fix it in XM360. Update the porting information (including the phone number) in XM360 and click Submit.

crumbs: Customer wants a new number instead?

crumbs: Switch a pending port to a new number
docs.text: Cancel a stuck or rejected port in XM360 by switching the device to a new phone number instead. Do this when the customer asks, or the old provider rejects the port. Canceling the port may affect promotions. Heads up: Let the customer know canceling the port may affect promotions.

docs.title: Switch to a new number
crumbs: Switch a pending port to a new number
docs.text: Heads up: Don't cancel a port and start a new port or new-number order directly in the RSSX/XM Network Management Tool. The order can fail with an Incomplete status and may need escalation to Verizon, our network partner. 3 steps.

steps.text: In XM360, select the device with the pending port.
Change the number option from Port to New Number, then click Confirm.
Click Submit. You'll see: The port request cancels on its own, and the device activates with a new phone number.

docs.title: Fix stuck orders from a system outage (R998)
crumbs: Fix stuck orders from a system outage (R998)
docs.text: Orders that fail with R998 during maintenance or an outage are queued and resubmit automatically — here's how to spot them and what to tell the customer. A planned or unplanned outage can make orders fail to provision. You may see: "R998: System outage or connectivity issues at Verizon, MPA Add Subscriber Fail.". This can show in XM360 or Customer Relationship Management (CRM). These orders are queued and resubmit automatically — you don't need to do anything. They can't activate until the maintenance or outage is over.

docs.title: Spot it in XM360
crumbs: Fix stuck orders from a system outage (R998)
docs.text: The R998 error shows on Devices when the order is first submitted. The error disappears if you leave and re-enter XM360 or switch tabs. This can happen if the customer calls back or a different rep loads the account in XM360. A second activation try may show Activation Processing, then Activating Pending. Activation Processing may show for a few minutes, followed by an Activating Pending message with no error.

docs.title: Spot it in CRM
crumbs: Fix stuck orders from a system outage (R998)
docs.text: The order stays at the Handle Fulfillment Response activity. The Fulfillment and Activations tabs show the R998 error. The Fulfillment tab also shows the order status. Fulfillment Systems Messages say "Wireless activation submitted" or "Order activation is in progress.". Find these on the View Order Action screen in the Fulfillment tab. It shows "Order is ready for activation" if the order was submitted but activation hasn't started.

docs.title: What to do
crumbs: Fix stuck orders from a system outage (R998)
docs.text: 2 steps.

steps.text: Tell the customer the outage affected their order. Let them know their activation or change order submits automatically once the issue is fixed.
Still stuck and can't be fixed? Open an XM Support case in ECM. Open Enterprise Case Management (ECM).; Click XM Support.; Pick Order Entry/Action Unavailable.

docs.title: Fix a failed credit card payment on an order
crumbs: Fix a failed credit card payment on an order
docs.text: When a new-service order is stuck because the card payment failed, update the card in XM360 so the order can ship. When a card fails, the customer doesn't get a shipping confirmation. The customer also gets an email about the failed charge. It says there was a problem charging the card and tells them to update their payment info or contact us. Unauthenticated customers can only retry the card on file. They can't change or add a new payment method. 2 steps.

steps.text: Find the customer's account and order in XM360. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.

Open the Billing tab to check the order status. You'll see: If a payment fails and stays pending more than a day, the tab shows an error asking to update the card, and the order shows "Waiting for Fulfillment.".

docs.title: Update the card
crumbs: Fix a failed credit card payment on an order
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: Tell the customer the payment failed and ask for updated card details. "Mr/Ms. Customer, there was a problem processing your credit card payment. I can help you fix this today. I will update your credit card information so we can finish your order.".
In XM360, select the Billing tab.
Click Manage payment method.
Select Update Card.
Enter the new card info and click Save. You'll see: The system processes the payment automatically. Once it's verified, the order proceeds as normal — nothing else to do.

docs.title: Unlock a phone in XM360
docs.text: Check a phone's Device Lock status in XM360 and unlock it so the customer can use another provider — or open an XM Unlocks case when XM360 can't. The account holder, primary user, or a Manager on the phone's original account. Most phones unlock automatically within 48 hours of becoming eligible. Applies to Xfinity Mobile and Comcast Business Mobile — not NOW Mobile. Always check the lock status first. Never unlock a phone that's already unlocked. The unlock policy tells you if a phone is eligible.

docs.title: Check the Device Lock status
docs.text: The first step is always the Device Lock status in XM360. Unlocked: Already unlocked in our system — help the customer verify on the phone. Apple: Open the Settings app. Tap General. Tap About. Scroll down to Carrier Lock. "No SIM restrictions" = unlocked. "SIM locked" or a company name = locked by the provider.; Android: Go to Settings. Tap Connections or Network & Internet. Tap Mobile Networks. Check Network Operators. If they can see and pick more than one provider, it's unlocked. Tip: If the phone shows locked or they can't verify, create an XM Unlocks case in Enterprise Case Management (ECM). If the customer says it's still locked, ask what phone they have and walk them through the check. Menu names vary by device. Request Sent: Unlocked on our side — the customer must finish their steps. See Help a customer finish a phone unlock. Locked: Scroll down and look at the Device Unlock button. Blue — eligible. Use the unlock steps below.; Gray — not eligible. See the unlock policy for details. Heads up: Don't open an XM Unlocks case unless the phone meets all policy requirements and isn't on an active line or isn't showing in XM360. Gray, but less than 48 hours since it became eligible on an active line? Tell the customer it should unlock automatically and they'll get an email when it does. Unknown: "Unknown" or not in XM360 — have the customer check the phone. Apple: Open the Settings app. Tap General. Tap About. Scroll down to Carrier Lock. "No SIM restrictions" = unlocked. "SIM locked" or a company name = locked by the provider.; Android: Go to Settings. Tap Connections…

docs.title: Unlock the phone
docs.text: Most unlocks are done in XM360 — no ECM case needed. 4 steps.

steps.text: Check the Device Status in XM360 for eligibility. A blue Unlock Device button means the phone can be unlocked and is active with Xfinity Mobile.

Have the customer confirm the IMEI (full or last four). If the phone has a physical IMEI and a digital SIM IMEI, confirm the physical IMEI.; The IMEI in XM360 must match the IMEI in the device settings.; It can be verified from device settings, or by screenshot if the phone was sold and the customer no longer has it.; Don't verify the IMEI in the Xfinity app — it may not match the device's real settings.; Check the IMEI's purchase order in XM360 is linked to the current account holder.
Make sure the customer's email on file is right.
Click Unlock Device. You'll see: An email with next steps goes to the customer. See Help a customer finish a phone unlock.

docs.title: Not eligible or not active
docs.text: Not eligible: Unlock Device is gray and shows the reason. Also check the unlock policy — it may help you find the reason. Eligible but not on an active line? Create an XM Unlocks case in ECM. In this case the Unlock Device button is grayed out.

docs.title: Open an XM Unlocks case
docs.text: The customer gets an email about the request within three business days. 4 steps.

steps.text: Check these first. Is the device already unlocked?; Are the device(s) paid off?; Has it been at least 60 days since the phone was bought? (Use the purchase or shipment date.); Is this a Military Suspension unlock? If yes, leave a note saying so.; Does the Xfinity Mobile account have a past-due balance?

Gather the account number, IMEI(s), reason and order number. Account number; IMEI(s); Reason for the unlock request (e.g., device deactivated, unlock button grayed out, request for unfreeze code); Order number — find the purchase order in XM360 and confirm it's for the current account holder.
Make sure XM360 has the customer's preferred email.
Open an XM Unlocks case in ECM.

Until they finish, XM360 shows Pending Unlock. The Device Unlock button says Unlock Requested.
When they finish, XM360 shows Unlocked.

steps.text: After you click Unlock Device, the customer gets an email with the code(s). The email has the phone's unlock code(s) and steps to follow.
The button changes to Device is already unlocked. Tip: This doesn't show the phone's real state — it just means the button was used and the code email was sent.
Customer puts a new physical SIM in the phone. You'll see: The phone asks for a "network unlock code.".
Customer taps the field above the line and enters the code.
Customer taps UNLOCK. Code lost or the phone froze? See Resend an unlock code or get an unfreeze code.

docs.text: Clicking Unlock Device sends an unlock signal to the phone. There's no code. 3 steps.

steps.text: Have the customer restart the phone. Most of the time a restart completes the unlock. If the phone asks for an unlock code, use the older Android steps above.
Look for the Carrier lock removed alert.
Some Pixel and Samsung phones say Your phone has been unlocked.

docs.title: Test the unlock (Android)
crumbs: Help a customer finish a phone unlock
docs.text: 4 steps.

steps.text: Restart the phone.
Put in another provider's SIM card.
On the Home screen, look for the "Phone Locked" message. This doesn't show automatically on the phone.

Make sure the phone is on cellular or WiFi. You'll see: Once connected, the unlock message shows in the notification panel. If it isn't connected when the unlock signal is sent, XM360 shows the status as pending.

docs.title: Motorola phones
crumbs: Help a customer finish a phone unlock
docs.text: Five failed unlock tries starts a three-minute cool-down. Restarting the phone during the cool-down resets the three-minute timer when it powers up. The phone says "Too many attempts, try again later.". All passcodes are discarded. After the timeout, five new tries are allowed on a new unlock request.

docs.title: Resend an unlock code or get an unfreeze code
crumbs: Resend an unlock code or get an unfreeze code
docs.text: Find an older Android phone's unlock code in XM360, resend it, or get the unfreeze code when too many wrong codes froze the unlock. 5 steps.

steps.text: Open the customer's account in XM360. In the store, find the account in Celestial Customer Space and launch XM360 from there. See Launch XM360.
Pick the phone that needs to be unlocked.
Go to Device Lock Status. You'll see: You'll see the unlock code and a link to resend the unlock request.
Too many wrong codes froze it? Click Resend unlock request. Entering the wrong code too many times freezes the unlock, and an unfreeze code is needed.

Read the Unfreeze Code to the customer. Heads up: Unfreeze codes are not emailed — you must tell the customer. Tip: The unlock code may not work on its own for some phones. Give these customers the unfreeze code and have them enter it instead.

docs.title: Fix voicemail problems
docs.text: First checks for Xfinity Mobile voicemail issues — data, updates, device-type feature codes and inbox limits — and when to escalate. Older Android phones use the Xfinity Mobile voicemail app. iPhones and newer Androids use the network partners' voicemail platform. All iPhones, plus Android phones released with or after the Samsung Galaxy S10 series. Retail reps can contact the Xfinity Mobile Center of Excellence (CoE) for voicemail support.

docs.title: What to do first
docs.text: 5 steps.

steps.text: Confirm mobile data is on. Voicemail needs the cellular data network. Confirm the member can use mobile data with WiFi turned off. Outside data coverage or with data off, they can't check voicemail or get notifications.
Confirm the phone software and voicemail app are updated.
Switched between Android and iPhone? Check the voicemail feature matches. Check the member's device type and use the feature code table below to confirm the right feature is on the line.
Confirm the inbox isn't over the size limit. Over the limit, they can't get new voicemail. For limits, review how to manage voicemail on my phone.
Launch the Xfinity Mobile Features issues ITG and pick Voicemail Issues. ITG = Interactive Troubleshooting Guide. Pick Voicemail Issues from the drop-down.

docs.title: Don'ts
docs.text: Never manually build a voicemail inbox in UMS. Never do a warranty exchange for a voicemail issue. A voicemail issue never involves a hardware failure that needs a new device. docs.title: Find a device's IMEI and ICCID
crumbs: Find a device's IMEI and ICCID
docs.text: Find the IMEI or ICCID on a phone, smartwatch or tablet — on the box, SIM tray, back of the device, in settings, or in XM360. IMEI and ICCID are unique IDs for phones, smartwatches and tablets. They identify a specific device on the mobile network. Find them on the box, on the device in XM360, or in settings. Works the same for Comcast Business Mobile customers.

docs.title: Before activation
crumbs: Find a device's IMEI and ICCID
docs.text: Check the package or the device itself. SIM tray: Phones and tablets: check the SIM tray. Apple: engraved on the tray for iPads with a SIM tray and iPhone 13 and older. For details, see Apple Support.; Google Pixel and Motorola: may be engraved on the tray for some phones. Box: All devices: check the barcode on the original box. The barcode shows the serial number, the EID and the IMEI/MEID. Back: iPads: the IMEI is etched on the back near the bottom. Most cellular-capable iPads. Back: Samsung and LG: IMEI and serial are printed on the back near the bottom. Printed in small text. Manufacturer help pages cover iPhones and iPads, Apple Watches, Samsung phones, tablets and watches, Google Pixel phones, tablets and watches, and Motorola phones.

docs.title: AT&T porting: good to know
docs.text: Wireless Account Lock blocks the port, SIM swaps and line changes. Any user with primary or secondary access can turn it off in the AT&T app. Only users with primary online access can request the PIN. Asking for a new PIN voids all earlier PINs. Update the port with the newest one. Give the carrier only the Number Transfer PIN, not the account passcode. Suspended accounts can only get a PIN online or in the app, not by text. Lost or broken phone: get the PIN online. AT&T says the device must be unlock-eligible first. Business accounts: only the primary user can request it, and not through *PORT or the app. FirstNet & Family accounts need a PIN; other FirstNet accounts don't. Tell the customer not to cancel AT&T first. A disconnected line must be reactivated before it can port.

docs.title: C³ Arcade
docs.text: Every game on the site on one screen — pick a cabinet and it opens right here. 6 games: C³ FOX RUN, AFTER HOURS, DEEP SIX, BLUFOX OVERDRIVE, BLUFOX CASINO, WINDY CITY DERBY.
asks: im on break what can i play

docs.title: C³ FOX RUN
docs.text: The break-room arcade cabinet. Run the fox, dodge the obstacles, hold the high score. Run the fox down the line, clear what the floor throws at you, and hold the high score.

docs.title: AFTER HOURS
docs.text: The second cabinet in the C³ arcade. When the floor is quiet, the break room is not. The lights are off and the store is yours. When the floor is quiet, the break room is not.

docs.title: DEEP SIX
docs.text: The third cabinet in the C³ arcade. Read the sonar, call the shot, and put the other fleet on the bottom. Blufox Fleet Command. Read the sonar, call the shot, and put the other fleet on the bottom.

docs.title: BLUFOX OVERDRIVE
docs.text: The fourth cabinet in the C³ arcade. Eight karts, six circuits, and a Chicago night that does not slow down. Eight karts, six circuits, one Chicago night. Tilt the phone to steer and hold the racing line.

docs.title: BLUFOX CASINO
docs.text: The fifth cabinet in the C³ arcade. Seven 3D tables dealt by Ace: blackjack, hold'em, roulette, slots, baccarat, craps and video poker — play chips only, nothing to buy and nothing to win. Seven 3D tables, one fox in a tuxedo. Blackjack, hold'em, roulette, baccarat, craps, slots and video poker. Play chips only.

docs.title: WINDY CITY DERBY
docs.text: The sixth cabinet in the C³ arcade. Pick one of six foxes and swing for the seats at Wrigley or Rate Field — ten outs a round, a daily challenge, and a company-wide leaderboard. Pick your fox, step in at Wrigley or Rate Field and put one on the street. Ten outs a round, plus a daily challenge on the company board.
